title: MySQL connect failure with fallback off aborts enable with a raw NPE
fix: In DatabaseConfig.ganglandDatabase, after setType(), check getDatabase()==null and throw a PluginException naming the MySQL settings (or catch RuntimeException around createSchema).
observation: With `Database.Type: mysql` and `Database.SQLite.Failed_MySQL: false`, a failed MySQL connect leaves `type == MYSQL` and `database == null`. The bean then calls `database.createSchema()` → `getDatabase().createSchema(...)` → **NPE**, which is not an `SQLException`/`IOException`, so it escapes the `catch` and aborts `onEnable` with a raw NPE instead of a diagnosable message.

title: Async autosave iterates the live user caches (CME, lost writes)
fix: Snapshot both caches on the main thread (a sync task copies the values to lists), then push only the DB write async; never call offlineUserManager.clear() off-thread.
observation: The autosave task runs on an async thread and iterates `userManager.getUsers().values()` / `offlineUserManager.getUsers().values()` and then calls `offlineUserManager.clear()`. `AbstractRepository.saveAll` also copies each supplier's live `map.values()` on that thread. A player joining/leaving concurrently can produce `ConcurrentModificationException` mid-save (partial save, some repositories skipped) or a lost write. Reproduce: heavy join/leave churn at the autosave tick.

title: Weapon-table wipe runs on the async thread while the main thread uses the cache
fix: Run resetWeapons on the main thread and push only the DELETE async; clear the cache after the save completes, not before.
tests: PluginDataCleanupServiceTest (covers the branch, not the threading)
location: `PluginDataCleanupService.java:98-108` reached from `PeriodicalUpdates.task()` on the async timer
observation: `resetWeapons()` deletes every `weapon` row and calls `weaponManager.clear()` from an async thread while the main thread may be reading/writing the weapon cache. Also, the very next step of the same tick saves weapons *from the now-empty cache*, so the wipe is immediately re-persisted — intended, but any weapon created between the clear and the save is lost.

title: DatabaseBackend Hikari pool is never disconnected on disable
fix: Keep the backend reference in GanglandDatabase and call backend.disconnect() from DatabaseManager.closeConnections() after forceUpdate().
observation: `DatabaseManager.closeConnections()` closes only the legacy `Database`. The `DatabaseBackend` (Mysql/Sqlite Hikari pool created in `GanglandDatabase.connectBackend`) is never disconnected on disable, leaking a pool and — on SQLite/Windows — file handles across a `/reload` or plugin-manager reload.

title: Unguarded shutdownBeans skips the final save and DB close if one bean throws
fix: Wrap context.shutdownBeans() and disableModules() in try/catch (log + Diagnostics) and run forceUpdate() and closeConnections() in a finally block.
observation: `context.shutdownBeans()` is unguarded: if any bean's `onShutdown()` throws, the final `PeriodicalUpdates.forceUpdate()` and `DatabaseManager.closeConnections()` never run — silent data loss on shutdown.

title: initialize()-style managers are never re-initialised by /glw reload
fix: Convert TurfManager, MailManager, ActiveBuffManager and GarrisonManager to BeanLifecycle (onPreClear/onInitialize) or have the reload pipeline call their initialize() explicitly.
observation: Managers that use the convention `public void initialize()` instead of `BeanLifecycle` are initialised once at bootstrap and are **never** cleared or re-initialised by `/glw reload`. Their caches go stale relative to reloaded YAML/DB state, and the reload is silently partial.

title: Dependency check (NBTAPI, Citizens) runs after the full bootstrap
fix: Move the required-plugin check to the top of onEnable, before new GanglandContext, so a missing dependency disables before files, DB and timers exist.
observation: Required-dependency validation (NBTAPI, Citizens) runs *after* `context.bootstrap()`, so on a server without them the plugin creates files, opens the DB, registers all listeners/commands and starts timers, and only then calls `disablePlugin`. Bootstrap may also have already crashed on a missing Citizens class.

title: Cleanup service constructed twice per reload pass
fix: Drop the duplicate initializeCleanupService() call from start(); keep the one in onInitialize.
observation: `onInitialize` builds a new timer and calls `initializeCleanupService()`, then `start()` calls `initializeCleanupService()` again — the cleanup service is constructed twice per pass. Also, when `Auto_Save.Enable` is turned **off** and then a reload happens, `repeatingTimer` stays `null` and `start()` returns before `initializeCleanupService()`… but `onInitialize` already ran it, so cleanup still works. Harmless today, but the duplicated call makes the invariant fragile.

title: Diagnostics hub static is never uninstalled on disable
fix: Uninstall (or install a no-op hub) in Gangland.onDisable after closeConnections so a stale DatabaseFaultSink is not left active.
observation: `Diagnostics.install(hub)` is a process-wide static that is never uninstalled on disable (unlike `ResourcePackTracker`). After a plugin-manager reload the old hub — holding a `DatabaseFaultSink` over a closed backend — stays `active()` until the new `KernelConfig` overwrites it, so faults raised during the gap hit a dead backend.

title: PlaceholderService.convert allocates a new provider chain per call
fix: Build the CompositePlaceholderProvider once and rebuild only when a resolver registers; synchronise the papiProvider assignment. Same fix as CM-28.
observation: `convert` allocates a new `ArrayList` and a new `CompositePlaceholderProvider` on **every** call, including per scoreboard line per tick. `papiProvider` is also lazily assigned without synchronisation.

title: PluginData id counter seeded to the last row id, so ids are reused and rows overwritten
fix: Seed PluginData.ID = max(id)+1 in PluginManager.initialize and make getNewId() safe.
observation: `PluginData.setID(pluginData.getId())` sets the static id counter to the id of the **last** loaded row, and `getNewId()` returns `ID++`. With more than one `plugin_data` row (or a non-zero id), the next `new PluginData(...)` reuses an existing id → the autosave upsert overwrites an existing row.

title: The "current" plugin_data record is whichever row loaded last
fix: Pick the record by max id (or keep exactly one row read by a fixed id), not list order.
observation: Both entry points use `dataList.get(dataList.size() - 1)`. `getPluginDataList()` is an unmodifiable view of an `ArrayList` whose order is DB row order — "the last one" is not a well-defined "current" record if more than one row ever exists.

title: /glw reload runs the whole save tick plus an offline SELECT on the main thread
fix: Keep the DB writes synchronous but load offline players async with a completion callback; or document the stall behind a flag.
observation: `/glw reload` runs the whole save tick (including a possible weapon-table `DELETE` via `checkAndPerformCleanup`) **on the main thread**, and `PlayerBootstrapService.loadOfflinePlayers` then does a synchronous `SELECT *` over `user`. On a large database this is a visible main-thread stall.

title: Two @Bean methods named repositoryRegistry return the same instance
fix: Delete the CONFIG-phase duplicate in DataConfig and inject the DATABASE-phase bean.
observation: Two `@Bean` methods both named `repositoryRegistry` produce the same `RepositoryRegistry` instance in different phases. `registerBean` overwrites the CONFIG-phase entry over the DATABASE-phase one under the same name and type. Harmless because the instance is identical, but it is a latent ambiguity if either ever returns a different object.

title: @ConditionalOnSetting is evaluated before Settings is loaded
fix: Evaluate conditions per phase (after FILE) in BeanFactory or make SettingsLookupImpl read lazily; add a test before any bean uses the annotation. Keystone upstream.
observation: `@ConditionalOnSetting` is evaluated in `BeanFactory.instantiate()` *before* any phase runs, when `Settings.getSettingsMap()` is still empty — every conditional would fail closed. No bean uses the annotation today, so this is a trap for future code, not a live bug.

title: Schema and table creation failures are only logged; the plugin runs without tables
fix: Treat createSchema/createTables failure as fatal in GanglandDatabase.initialize (throw PluginException, disable). Keystone upstream: DatabaseHelper.runQueries.
observation: `createSchema()`/`createTables()`/`insertInitialData()` failures are caught inside `runQueries` and only logged. The plugin then runs against a database with missing tables; the first symptom is a repository `SQLException` routed to `gangland_faults` (which itself may not exist).

title: A repository whose constructor throws surfaces later as "No repository registered"
fix: Rethrow (or collect and fail bootstrap) in RepositoryRegistry.scanAndRegisterRepositories instead of WARN-and-skip. Keystone upstream.
observation: A repository whose constructor throws is logged at WARN and skipped. The failure surfaces much later as `IllegalStateException: No repository registered for: X` from a manager's `initialize()`, aborting bootstrap with a misleading message.

title: insertInitialData returns silently when the rank repositories are missing
fix: Log at ERROR and throw when the head/tail rank cannot be inserted on a fresh install.
observation: `insertInitialData()` returns silently when the rank repositories are absent or of an unexpected type, so a fresh install can end up with no head/tail rank and no diagnostic.

title: Settings helpers silently substitute defaults (verified correct code)
fix: No code change; optionally add key-level WARN lines through ConfigReport for missing sections.
observation: The scalar helpers (`str/intVal/dbl/money/bool/strList/intList`) all silently substitute a hard-coded default when the section or key is missing, and `section()` returns `null` for an absent mapping. A typo'd or removed YAML section therefore produces working-but-wrong values with only a single aggregated `ConfigReport` line at INFO/WARN — no key-level failure. Verified correct code; the risk is operational, not a defect.

title: A bad Language value on reload disables the plugin mid-reload
fix: LanguageLoader.initialize should fall back to the previous or English file and report, never call disablePlugin from a reload pass. Keystone upstream.
observation: `LanguageLoader` is a `BeanLifecycle`, so `/glw reload` does re-read `Language`. But if the new value names a non-existent message file, `initialize()` logs and calls `disablePlugin(plugin)` **from inside the reload pass** — the plugin disables mid-`reloadLifecycleBeans()`, with the remaining beans' `onInitialize(false)` still to run and `onDisable()` firing against a half-cleared graph.

title: updateAllData builds a fresh TableBackend per call and bypasses processSave
fix: Reuse repository.tableBackend() (or call repository.saveAll) so processSave pre-processing applies.
observation: `updateAllData` constructs a fresh `TableBackend<>` per call rather than reusing the repository's cached one; minor allocation, but it also bypasses any `processSave()` pre-processing that `AbstractRepository.saveAll` would apply to `User`/`Bank`.

title: /glw reload inventory calls an empty resetCache()
fix: Remove resetCache() and its call, or implement it.
observation: `/glw reload inventory` calls `PeriodicalUpdates.resetCache()`, which does nothing. Dead code path that reads like a real step.

title: Both UserManager beans register data suppliers on the same repositories
fix: Give the offline manager its own supplier registration (or merge both caches into one supplier) so RepositoryRegistry.saveAll persists both. Same root as US-12.
observation: Both the `online` and `offline` `UserManager` beans call `setDataSupplier` on the **same** `UserRepository` and `BankRepository` instances, so the second one to initialise silently overwrites the first. `RepositoryRegistry.saveAll()` therefore persists only one of the two caches. Today this is masked because `PeriodicalUpdates.updatingDatabase` upserts both caches directly *and* clears the offline cache before `saveAll()` runs — but any other caller of `UserRepository.saveAllFromMemory()` (or a reorder of those two statements) silently drops one cache.

title: Bean order is JVM-dependent for beans with equal dependency sets
fix: Sort bean definitions by name (stable) in BeanFactory/BeanGraph; keep parameter edges for real ordering. Keystone upstream.
location: Keystone `BeanFactory.java:190` (`configClass.getDeclaredMethods()`) + `BeanGraph.topologicalSort` Kahn seeding by list order
observation: Bean definitions are collected in JVM-unspecified `getDeclaredMethods()` order, and the `@Configuration` classes themselves come from an unordered `Set` out of `ReflectionUtil.findClasses`. Beans with identical dependency sets therefore have **non-deterministic** relative order across JVMs/recompiles. Combined with #23, which of the two `UserManager`s wins the shared data supplier is not stable. The codebase's documented "add a parameter to encode ordering" convention is the only defence.

title: offlineUserManager.clear() runs before repositoryRegistry.saveAll()
fix: Reorder: saveAll first, then clear; add a test pinning the order.
observation: `offlineUserManager.clear()` runs **before** `repositoryRegistry.saveAll()`. Any repository whose supplier reads the offline cache (see #23) sees an empty collection at that point. Ordering-sensitive by accident, not by design.

title: NPE on every join when Update_Checker.Enable is false
fix: Null-check updateChecker in CreateAccountListener (or always construct the checker in a disabled state).
observation: `updateCheckerInitializer()` returns early when `Update_Checker.Enable: false`, leaving `updateChecker` null; the LOWEST-priority `PlayerJoinEvent` handler dereferences it unconditionally
impact: NPE on every join with the updater disabled — thrown before `userManager.add(user)`, so the whole account-creation handler aborts and the player has no cached `User`

title: /glw <sub> help bypasses the subcommand permission
fix: Route onSubHelp through runExecute, or check sender.hasPermission(sub.getPermission()) before renderHelp.
observation: `onSubHelp` calls `renderHelp` directly, never `runExecute` — no `sender.hasPermission(sub.getPermission())` check
impact: Anyone with `gangland.command.main` can read every subcommand's full help page (usage strings for admin/dev commands included) by typing `/glw <sub> help`

title: GangCommand never registers: condition "isGangEnabled" never matches
fix: Change the annotation to condition="gangEnabled" (the field key) or make SettingsLookupImpl also resolve getter names.
observation: `@CommandHandler(condition = "isGangEnabled")` is a getter *method* name, but the command-side lookup is a `settingsMap` lookup keyed by *field* names (`gangEnabled`); the listener side (`ListenerManager.invokeMethod`) resolves method names reflectively
impact: `settingsMap.get("isGangEnabled")` is always null → `isEnabled` returns false → **`GangCommand` is never registered**, so `/glw gang` does not exist (dispatch falls into the "did you mean" branch). Silent — `CommandService` just `continue`s

title: /glw resource is gated on the scoreboard toggle
fix: Replace Settings.isScoreboardEnabled() with Settings.isResourcePackEnabled() in DownloadResourceCommand.
tests: FIXED Gangland 0.10.0 WS1 G3, commit 02f334b3 (branch 0.10.0): DownloadResourceCommand.java now reads Settings.isResourcePackEnabled(); the scoreboard toggle it used to read no longer exists - the whole scoreboard system (including Settings.isScoreboardEnabled()) was deleted in the same gate, replaced by the standalone Plaque plugin. Pinning tests for the old scoreboard module were deleted with it (ScoreboardTest/LineTest), not flipped.
observation: The resource-pack re-send is gated on `Settings.isScoreboardEnabled()`; the resource-pack toggle is `Settings.isResourcePackEnabled()` (used correctly in `LoadResourcePackListener.java:27,74`)
impact: `/glw resource` silently does nothing when scoreboards are off, and pushes the pack when the pack feature is off

title: Balance tab-completion runs a full user-table SELECT per keystroke on the main thread
fix: Complete from the online/offline UserManager caches, and resolve the target in the action body from the cache first.
observation: The `OptionalArgument` completion supplier runs `UserTable.selectAllTableQuery` and `Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(uuid)` for **every** registered user, synchronously, on **every tab keystroke**
impact: Main-thread DB query + N `OfflinePlayer` lookups per keypress; on a large user table this is a visible server freeze. The same scan runs again in the action body (89-118)

title: Console tab-complete of /glw option throws ClassCastException and spams gang-less players
fix: Guard sender instanceof Player in the completion supplier and drop the chat message.
observation: The completion supplier casts `(Player) sender` and calls `user.sendMessage(Messages.MUST_CREATE_GANG…)`
impact: Console tab completion throws `ClassCastException` inside `CommandTabCompleter` (unguarded there); a gang-less player is spammed with a chat message on every TAB press

title: (Player) sender casts in a console-allowed command
fix: Mark ComponentExecutorCommand user=true or guard every action with an instanceof check. Same as GR-36.
observation: `(Player) sender` casts in argument actions of a `user=false` command (`option`)
impact: Console running `/glw option gang rank …` throws CCE; `Argument.execute` catches it and sends the sender `throwable.getMessage()` — for a CCE that message is the internal class-cast text, leaking implementation detail

title: Throwable messages are sent verbatim to players
fix: Send a generic Messages error and log the real message; pass through only PluginException messages. Keystone upstream.
observation: `sender.sendMessage(message != null ? message : actionError())` sends any throwable's message verbatim to the player
impact: Internal exception text (SQL messages, class names, file paths) can reach players. Intentional per the javadoc ("throw with a player-facing message"), but it is unfiltered

title: Dispatch-level Throwable is only logged; the sender sees nothing and Diagnostics is skipped
fix: Match Keystone: report to Diagnostics.active() and send CommandMessages.dispatchError().
observation: Gangland's `catch (Throwable)` only calls `log.error(...)`; Keystone's version also reports to `Diagnostics` and sends `CommandMessages.dispatchError()` to the sender
impact: Dispatch-level bugs are not persisted in `gangland_faults` and the sender sees nothing at all — the command appears to do nothing

title: commands.json has 19 dead entries and reload data/inventory/cleanup drift
fix: Delete the dealer/kit/safe_wand/spawn/warp entries; fix the reload_* entries to match ReloadCommand.initializeArguments.
tests: InformationManagerTest (drift test; update the count when cleaned)
observation: 19 dead entries (`dealer*`, `kit*`, `safe_wand`, `spawn*`, `warp*`) for commands that no longer exist; `reload_database` documents a `/glw reload data` argument that `ReloadCommand.initializeArguments` does not create; `reload_inventory`/`reload_cleanup` are missing for arguments that do exist
impact: `/glw reload help` advertises a non-existent `data` argument and omits `inventory`/`cleanup`. The dead entries are inert (no command filters on those prefixes) but mislead maintainers

title: Teleport and Waypoint commands consume the same 17 help entries
fix: Give TeleportCommand its own teleport_* entries and filter by that prefix.
observation: Two commands consume the same 17 JSON entries
impact: `/glw help` lists all 17 waypoint lines twice; `/glw teleport help` shows waypoint usage strings

title: HelpCommand aggregate list is built without sender or permission filtering
fix: Build the list per sender (permission + dev visibility) at execution time.
observation: Position-1 completion filters by permission **and** visibility, so nothing leaks there; but `CommandManager.onCommand`'s unknown-subcommand suggestion (85-97) also uses `permissibleCommands`, which is permission-gated — so no leak on that path either. However `HelpCommand`'s aggregate list is built once at construction from `commandView()` with **no sender and no filter** (`command/sub/HelpCommand.java:28-35`)
impact: Any command that contributed `HelpInfo` entries is visible to every sender in `/glw help`, regardless of permission or the dev filter. Today all five dev-filtered classes have empty `HelpInfo`, so nothing leaks — but adding one help line to a dev command would expose it to everyone

title: /glw debug settings prints the MySQL password
fix: Redact mysqlPassword/mysqlUsername/mysqlHost (any key containing password or secret) in the settings dump.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 wave 3, commit 8a731fd5 (branch worktree-p0-wave-3); SettingsRedaction filters the debug dump AND GanglandPlaceholder; SettingsRedactionTest
observation: `/glw debug settings` dumps `Settings.getSettingsMap()`, which is built by reflection over every static field — including `mysqlHost`, `mysqlUsername`, `mysqlPassword` (`Settings.java:42`)
impact: Anyone holding `gangland.command.debug.settings` (or an op) can print the database password to chat/console

title: TimerCommand map keyed by the live CommandSender is never cleared
fix: Key by UUID and remove (and stop the SequenceTimer) on PlayerQuitEvent.
observation: `Map<CommandSender, SequenceTimer>` keyed by the live `CommandSender` (a `Player`), never cleared on quit
impact: Strong reference to `Player` objects — a classic Bukkit memory leak, and `SequenceTimer`s of departed players keep running

title: message_es.yml is missing 114 message paths
fix: Add the missing keys (turf, banker, invite, ally, shop) or make LanguageLoader fall back to message_en for missing paths.
observation: 114 declared `Messages` paths are absent; the jar fallback is the same-language file, so there is no English fallback
impact: Spanish servers render `<missing: Commands.Turf…>` for the entire turf, banker, gang-invite/ally-pending and shop-sell feature sets. `LanguageLoader` logs 114 WARN lines on every load/reload

title: Only 4 of 9 ArgumentMessages slots are localised
fix: Install confirmRequired, confirmPrompt, didYouMean, selectorSyntax and selectorNoPlayer from Messages in GanglandContext.
observation: Only 4 of Keystone's 9 `ArgumentMessages` slots are installed
impact: `confirmRequired`, `confirmPrompt` (seen on `/glw update download`), `didYouMean` (seen on every typo), `selectorSyntax`, `selectorNoPlayer` remain hard-coded English on a Spanish server

title: Any "help" token anywhere in the line renders help instead of executing
fix: Treat "help" as help only when it is args[0] or args[1].
observation: `Arrays.stream(args).anyMatch("help"::equalsIgnoreCase)` matches the token anywhere in the line
impact: Any command taking free text can be hijacked: `/glw gang rename help`, `/glw gang description … help …` render a help page instead of executing

title: Suggestions always say /glw even via the /gangland alias
fix: Pass the typed label to runExecute.
observation: `runExecute(shortPrefix, …)` passes the constant `"glw"` instead of the typed `label`
impact: A player using the `/gangland` alias gets "did you mean `/glw …`" suggestions; cosmetic drift from Keystone, which passes `label`

title: Help page-range errors are raw English
fix: Use Commands.Syntax.Page_Invalid through Messages in HelpInfo.
tests: HelpInfoTest (pins the text; update when localised)
observation: Page-range errors are raw English `IllegalArgumentException` messages surfaced through `errorMessage(...)`; `message_en.yml` has an unused `Commands.Syntax.Page_Invalid` key
impact: Untranslated user-facing text while a suitable message key sits unused

title: Missing general/general_page JSON keys put null in the help list (NPE)
fix: Null-check the two lookups and log a clear error.
observation: `informationManager.getCommands().get("general")` / `get("general_page")` are added without a null check
impact: A removed/renamed JSON key puts `null` in the help list → NPE inside `HelpInfo.displayHelp` (`list.get(index).toString()`), which is caught only if it is an `IllegalArgumentException` — an NPE escapes to `Argument.execute`'s Throwable catch

title: parallelStream over the command registry during construction
fix: Use a plain stream.
observation: `parallelStream()` over `commandView()` during construction
impact: Registry mutation during construction (LOWEST priority makes it the last command, so in practice safe) plus needless fork-join use at bootstrap

title: A missing or malformed commands.json kills bootstrap with no message
fix: Catch and rethrow as PluginException("commands.json missing/invalid") with the path.
observation: `Objects.requireNonNull(Gangland.class.getResourceAsStream("/commands.json"))` with no try/catch, running in the KERNEL phase
impact: A missing or malformed `commands.json` throws during bootstrap and takes the whole plugin down with no actionable message

title: InformationManager is a static on the command base
fix: Documented trade-off; inject per command when Keystone 2.0 lands.
observation: `InformationManager` is a `static` field on the command base
impact: Process-wide static on a shared classloader; a second consumer or a re-bootstrap would clobber it. Documented as a deliberate trade-off in the javadoc

title: Developer UUIDs hard-coded in DevCommandVisibilityFilter
fix: Move the list to settings.yml.
observation: Two developer UUIDs hard-coded in shipped source
impact: Not a security hole (visibility only), but it ships personal identifiers and cannot be configured by server owners

title: FAILED_DOWNLOAD and DECLINED never call markUnloaded
fix: Call markUnloaded(player) in both branches.
observation: `FAILED_DOWNLOAD` and `DECLINED` never call `markUnloaded`
impact: A player who had the pack, reloaded, then declined stays marked "loaded", so `SoundEffect.CUSTOM` plays silence for them

title: The DECLINED fallback button runs a dev-filtered command players cannot use
fix: Point the button at a player-visible command (e.g. /glw resource) or give it its own permission.
observation: The DECLINED fallback button runs `/glw option click resource`, whose permission is `gangland.command.option` and which is dev-filtered
impact: Ordinary players clicking the offered button get `Messages.COMMAND_NO_PERM`

title: /glw update throws NPE when the updater is disabled
fix: Null-check getUpdateChecker() and send an "updater disabled" message.
observation: `getUpdateChecker().getLatestVersion()` with no null guard
impact: `/glw update` with the updater disabled → NPE → caught by `Argument.execute` → the player sees the generic action-error line

title: Placeholder provider chain is rebuilt on every convert call
fix: Cache the CompositePlaceholderProvider; rebuild only when resolvers change.
observation: A new `ArrayList` + N lambda wrappers + a new `CompositePlaceholderProvider` (with `List.copyOf`) are allocated on **every** `convert` call
impact: `convert` runs per scoreboard line per tick per player and per inventory item render — measurable allocation churn on a busy server. The chain is immutable once resolvers stop registering and could be cached

title: Resolver lambda ignores the composite's offlinePlayer argument
fix: Use the argument the composite passes.
observation: The resolver lambda ignores the composite's `offlinePlayer` argument and closes over the outer `player`
impact: Correct for the current call sites (a `Player` is always passed) but means an offline-capable provider inserted into the chain would silently receive the wrong subject

title: Placeholder branch uses contains() instead of startsWith()
fix: Use startsWith.
observation: `param.contains("user_")`/`"bank_"`/`"gang_"` instead of `startsWith`
impact: A PAPI token such as `%someplugin_user_x%` that survived to this link enters the wrong branch (it falls through, so the effect is a wasted lookup, not a wrong value)

title: Unresolvable placeholders render as "NA"
fix: Return null so the token stays visible as %typo%.
observation: Unresolvable tokens return the literal `"NA"`
impact: A typo'd placeholder renders as `NA` on scoreboards/lore instead of remaining visible as `%typo%`, making config mistakes hard to spot

title: Placeholder resolution has no main-thread guard
fix: Guard with Bukkit.isPrimaryThread() and either reschedule or read immutable snapshots.
observation: Resolution touches `memberManager`, `gangManager`, `userManager` and `Bukkit` state with no thread guard
impact: Any async caller (a PAPI expansion invoked from an async chat/scoreboard task) reads live manager collections off the main thread. No async call site was found in this area, but nothing prevents one — placeholders are also resolved from PAPI, whose callers are outside our control

title: TimeMessages singleton may be vestigial
fix: Verify Keystone consumes TimeMessagesProvider; delete the class if not.
observation: `initialize()` is a no-op once the singleton exists, and nothing found installs the provider into Keystone
impact: The class may be vestigial; verify whether any Keystone seam consumes `TimeMessagesProvider`

title: gangland-core feature.Executor has no subclass
fix: Delete it.
observation: Abstract class with no subclass anywhere in the repo
impact: Dead code in `gangland-core`

title: Keystone process-wide statics (ArgumentMessages, CommandManager.defaultInstance)
fix: Keystone 2.0 item; no Gangland action.
observation: Process-wide statics on the shared Keystone classloader
impact: Documented Keystone limitation until 2.0.0; a second Keystone consumer on the same server would fight over the localized strings

title: Reload success/failure text is hard-coded English
fix: Route through Messages keys.
observation: Reload success/failure text is hard-coded English built with `&` codes, not `Messages` keys
impact: Untranslated operator-facing output

title: gangland.command.main and every framework-registered command node default to OP, so a non-op player cannot run /glw on a fresh install
fix: W1-K kickoff (orchestrator-owned plugin.yml): add a permissions: block with default: true for the player verbs (gangland.command.main, map, gang and the gang player sub-verbs, turf info and list); admin and destructive nodes stay OP, and Argument.addPermission skips names already declared. Record the behaviour change in the 0.14.0 migration doc. Covering tests: NEW PluginYmlPermissionsTest (player set default true, gangland.turf.admin not). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W1-K of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
location: gangland-impl src/main/resources/plugin.yml:20-28; command/CommandManager.java:56-59; Keystone keystone-command argument/Argument.java:111-120
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] plugin.yml declares /glw with permission gangland.command.main and declares only that node, default op (L27-28). Keystone Argument.addPermission registers every other command node with new Permission(name), whose Bukkit default is OP, and CommandManager.onCommand refuses a sender without gangland.command.main. Without a permissions plugin granting gangland.command.* (GangPermissions' Javadoc says players are expected to be granted it) a non-op player cannot run /glw at all. Read from code; not run on a fresh server.

title: /glw module install gang and install lootchest fail: ModuleInstalls.OFFICIAL lists six ids and omits two shipped modules
fix: W6-K: add gang (org.luckyraven:gangland-gang), lootchest (org.luckyraven:gangland-lootchest) and the new fights id to ModuleInstalls.OFFICIAL, moving from Map.of to Map.ofEntries because Map.of stops at ten pairs; update the six-ids javadoc and the HostApi/README lists. [found by the Gangs+ parity pass 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W6-K of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
tests: ModuleInstallsTest for gang, lootchest and fights (unknown today)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, Gangs+ parity pass; code-checked against master] OFFICIAL is Map.of with six entries (mail, turf, civilians, copsncrooks, gadget, npcshops). gangland-gang and gangland-lootchest both ship a module.yml (Ids gang and lootchest) and mail and turf declare Depends: gang, so a server that installs turf or mail through /glw module install cannot obtain the module they need by its short id; only the full group:artifact coordinate works. Read from code; not run.

title: documentation/features/jail-detainment.md:3 and features/wanted-bounty.md:3 link to the deleted wearables.md and weapons.md (dead since 0.9.0)
fix: Open: drop the dead nav links.
observation: [found 2026-10-05 by the Cops N Crooks 0.15 wave on branch cnc-lose-them; confirmed present on master 16d1f064] Navigation footer still points at pages that left the repo with the weapon module.

title: hasUniqueItem is inverted: the duplicate guard never fires and phones multiply on every join
fix: Return true when the item matches (remove the continue) and compare by the uniqueItem NBT tag (see IT-03).
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 c94fceab (#8); UniqueItemUtilTest + UniqueItemIdentityIntegrationTest now assert the fix
observation: `hasUniqueItem` does `if (uniqueItem.compareTo(item) == 0) continue;` — it **skips** the matching item and returns `true` only for a *different* unique item of the same material. The predicate is inverted.
impact: The `Allow_Duplicates: false` guard in `LoadUniqueItem:46` and `:89` never fires, so a fresh copy is granted on every join, respawn and undown; with `Overrides: false` each copy lands in the next free slot, filling the inventory with phones.

title: removeItem nulls the first slot that does NOT match
fix: Invert the condition so only the matching slot is cleared; match by NBT tag.
observation: `removeItem` has the same inversion: `if (uniqueItem.compareTo(contents[i]) == 0) continue;` then `inventory.setItem(i, null)`. It nulls the first slot that does **not** match.
impact: Silent destruction of an arbitrary inventory slot when a player is downed while holding a droppable unique item.

title: compareTo compares the raw &-coded config name to the built display name
fix: Implement identity via UniqueItemKeys.UNIQUE_ITEM_KEY on the stack and drop the display-name comparison.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 c94fceab (#10); UniqueItemTest matches_*/compareTo_* now assert tag identity
observation: `compareTo` compares the raw config `name` (`&`-codes, unresolved placeholders) with `meta.getDisplayName()` (§-translated, placeholders resolved by `ItemBuilder.setDisplayName` → `ChatUtil.color`).
impact: The comparison effectively never returns 0 for a real built stack, so the two bugs above always take their wrong branch. Identity should read the `uniqueItem` NBT tag.

title: AmmunitionConverter drops a custom name when the template has no lore
fix: Capture meta after applyAttributes (or apply the attributes to the final ItemBuilder).
observation: `meta` is captured **before** `applyAttributes` and written back afterwards when the original had no lore.
impact: `ammunition:x{name=Custom}` silently loses the custom name (and any colour) for ammo whose template has no lore.

title: Serializer order (UNIQUE first) contradicts refresher order (WEAPON first)
fix: Put UNIQUE first in both registries so a unique wrapper survives a refresh.
observation: Serializer order puts UNIQUE first ("unique wins over the wrapped domain"), refresher order puts WEAPON/WEARABLE before UNIQUE.
impact: A unique item that also carries a weapon/wearable tag is *identified* as unique but *rebuilt* as a plain weapon, dropping the `uniqueItem` tag on every shop delivery.

title: decorate() resets custom NBT runtime state (ammo, fuel, owner) to factory values
fix: Override decorate in the weapon, car and unique refreshers to carry over ammo-left, fuel_current and car_owner.
observation: `decorate` restores only vanilla damage and enchantments; custom NBT runtime state (weapon ammo counter, `fuel_current`, use counters, `car_owner`) is reset to factory values.
impact: Sell / trade-in flows treat a spent item as pristine — a possible value exploit and a state-loss bug. The javadoc explicitly asks implementations to override; none do.

title: Non-movable unique items can be moved via drag or number-key swap
fix: Handle InventoryDragEvent and hotbar/offhand swaps in UniqueItemInventoryRestrict.
observation: Only `InventoryClickEvent` is handled; `InventoryDragEvent` is absent, and a hotbar number-key swap while a container is open clicks the *top* inventory, so the swapped hotbar slot is never inspected.
impact: Non-`Movable` unique items can be moved into containers via drag or number-key swap.

title: Drop_On_Death=false items are destroyed on death instead of kept
fix: Keep non-dropping unique items and re-add them on respawn; honour Drop_On_Death under KEEP_INVENTORY too.
observation: With `KEEP_INVENTORY` on, **all** unique items are removed from `getDrops()` regardless of `Drop_On_Death`. Without it, items with `dropOnDeath == false` are removed from drops, which destroys them (they are not returned to the player).
impact: An item with `Drop_On_Death: false` and `Add_On_Respawn: false` is permanently lost on death.

title: UniqueItemAddon skips bad entries and falls back to BARRIER silently
fix: log.warn each skipped key and reject unresolvable materials instead of substituting BARRIER.
observation: Three silent `continue`s (no `Inventory` section, no `Material`, no `Name`) and `orElse(XMaterial.BARRIER)` at `:119`. Nothing is logged at WARN.
impact: An admin typo makes an item vanish from the registry or become a BARRIER with no diagnostic.

title: XMaterial.get() may return null and NPE at build time
fix: Check for null and skip the item with a warning.
observation: `material.get()` (XMaterial → Material) can return `null` on a server where the material does not exist; the result is passed straight into `UniqueItem.material`.
impact: `new ItemBuilder(null)` → `new ItemStack(null)` NPE the first time the item is built.

title: Attribute values cannot contain commas, so multi-line lore is unreachable
fix: Let KEY_VALUE_PATTERN accept quoted values (or use ; as the lore separator) and document it.
observation: `KEY_VALUE_PATTERN` value class is `[^,}]+`, so any attribute value containing a comma truncates — including the multi-line `lore` that `ItemAttributes.java:29` splits on commas.
impact: Multi-line lore via `{lore=a,b}` is unreachable through `ItemParser`; only the first line survives.

title: A second {...} group is stripped but never parsed
fix: Parse every group (merge attributes) or reject a second group loudly.
observation: `matcher.replaceAll("")` strips **every** `{…}` group, but only the first was parsed.
impact: A second attribute group is silently discarded.

title: Material fallback uses raw Material.valueOf instead of XMaterial
fix: Resolve through XMaterial.matchXMaterial in ItemParser.getConverter.
observation: `Material.valueOf(type)` (raw enum) decides the material fallback, while `MaterialConverter:17` resolves through XMaterial.
impact: A material name XMaterial can resolve but the running `Material` enum cannot (legacy/renamed) is rejected before it reaches the converter.

title: Documented DSL attributes (custom_model_data, amount, enchantments...) are ignored
fix: Implement the advertised attributes in ItemAttributes or remove them from the javadoc.
observation: Supported attributes are only `name`, `lore`, `color`. `ItemDslAdapter`'s javadoc (`:29`) advertises `custom_model_data`, and no converter reads `amount`, enchantments, item flags, unbreakable or skull texture.
impact: Documented DSL attributes are silently ignored (and now flagged as `dsl.unknown_attr`); NBT/model-data cannot be expressed in an item reference.

title: color accepts only Color enum names on leather armour
fix: Accept hex values and support PotionMeta/MapMeta; log on failure.
observation: `color` accepts only Keystone `Color` enum names, only on `LeatherArmorMeta`, and swallows `IllegalArgumentException`.
impact: Hex colours and non-leather dyed items fail silently.

title: ItemDslAdapter has no production caller
fix: Wire ItemDslAdapter into the shop, loot and unique parsers so located errors reach the ConfigReport, or delete it.
observation: Referenced only from `ItemDslAdapterTest`; no production caller and no `@Bean` in `ItemConfig`.
impact: The located-error path advertised in the javadoc is not actually in use — every production item reference still fails silently via `ItemParser`.

title: Gangland ships a parallel copy of Keystone's item framework
fix: Migrate to keystone-item's ItemParser and registries (tracked migration item).
observation: Keystone 1.7.3 ships a parallel `ItemParser`/`ItemKind`/`ItemConverterRegistry`/`ItemSerializerRegistry`/`ItemRefresher*`/`MaterialItemSerializer` (plus `StandardItemKind`) that Gangland does not import.
impact: Two diverging copies of the same framework; Keystone's copy has unit tests the Gangland copy lacks. Adoption is a pending migration item.

title: hasTag predicates run on AIR and trigger six NBT reads plus warn spam
fix: Return false early for AIR/null in ItemPredicates.hasTag.
observation: `hasTag` does not guard AIR; `ItemSerializerRegistry` calls up to six predicates before the MATERIAL catch-all.
impact: Serializing an AIR stack triggers six NBTAPI reads that `ReflectiveNbtApiAccessor:120-131` catches and `log.warn`s — potential log spam in shop matching loops.

title: refresh/decorate return the source instance for null or AIR
fix: Return a clone (or null) so no shared instance can leak.
observation: `refresh`/`decorate` return the **source instance** (not a clone) for null/AIR, contradicting the class javadoc's "call-sites can always rely on getting a safe-to-deliver copy".
impact: A shared instance can leak into a player inventory if a shop entry is AIR.

title: Serialised ids are lowercased unconditionally
fix: Keep the case, or make registry lookups case-insensitive end to end.
observation: The extracted value is lowercased unconditionally.
impact: A registry key with uppercase characters serialises to an id that `ItemParser` cannot convert back.

title: addItemToInventory returns false on success
fix: Return addItem(...) directly and fix any caller.
observation: `addItemToInventory` returns `!addItem(...)` — `false` on success.
impact: No caller reads it today, but the inverted contract is a trap for the next caller.

title: Interaction is blocked whenever the item is not Movable
fix: Add a separate Usable flag, or block only moving, not right-click.
observation: Interaction is blocked when `!isMovable()`.
impact: Conflates inventory mobility with usability: an item pinned to a slot can never be right-clicked.

title: Literal "uniqueItem" instead of the UniqueItemKeys constant in four places
fix: Replace with UniqueItemKeys.UNIQUE_ITEM_KEY.
observation: The literal `"uniqueItem"` is used instead of `UniqueItemKeys.UNIQUE_ITEM_KEY` in four places.
impact: Renaming the constant silently breaks the listeners.

title: InventoryParser reads Action from Open.Event while the YAML nests it under OnItemClick
fix: Read Open.Event.OnItemClick.Action and fix phone.yml's RIGHT_CLICK value (see UI-20).
observation: `parseActions` reads `Action` from the `Open.Event` section; the YAML nests it under `Open.Event.OnItemClick`.
impact: The configured `Action:` is dead config; the fallback (`RIGHT_CLICK_AIR` + `RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK`) always applies, so `LEFT_CLICK` handlers cannot be configured.

title: /glw item unique give accepts zero and negative amounts
fix: Validate amount >= 1 and send a usage error.
observation: `slots = ceil(amount / maxStackSize)`; a zero or negative amount yields a zero-length array and an empty `addItem`, yet `giveUniqueItem` still returns `true`.
impact: `/glw item unique give phone -5` reports "Gave phone x-5".

title: item_unique_info is documented with an argument it does not take
fix: Fix the commands.json usage string.
observation: Documented as `info <name>`; the implementation reads the main-hand item and accepts no argument.
impact: Misleading help text.

title: UniqueItemAddon.clear leaves the FuelService registry populated
fix: Clear fuel definitions for unique items in clear() (or FuelService.onPreClear).
observation: `clear()` empties the item map but leaves `FuelService`'s registry populated.
impact: Fuel definitions for items deleted from the YAML survive a reload.

title: gangland.uniqueitem.<key> permissions are registered but never checked
fix: Enforce them in LoadUniqueItem and the give command, or stop registering them.
observation: `gangland.uniqueitem.<key>` permissions are registered but never checked anywhere in the codebase.
impact: Dead permission surface; admins may assume it gates the item.

title: Respawn inventory write at default priority may be overwritten
fix: Delay the give by one tick in onRespawn.
observation: `PlayerRespawnEvent` is handled at default priority and writes to the inventory synchronously during the event.
impact: On some server builds inventory writes during `PlayerRespawnEvent` are overwritten by the respawn itself — unverified here.

title: Without NBTAPI the whole identity layer silently disables
fix: Keep NBTAPI a hard dependency and fail loudly if NbtBridge is the no-op accessor at bootstrap.
observation: Without NBTAPI, `addTag` is dropped and `hasNBTTag` returns `false` for everything.
impact: The entire unique-item, weapon, wearable, car and money identity layer silently disables; `plugin.yml` lists NBTAPI as a hard dependency, so this only bites if the plugin's shape changes.

title: Ammo fallback matches by display name and material
fix: Require the ammo NBT tag; drop the name-based fallback.
observation: Fallback matching by coloured display name + material when the ammo NBT tag is missing.
impact: Two ammo types sharing a material and display name are indistinguishable; a player-renamed vanilla stack can be mistaken for ammo.

title: Car and fuel refresh rebuilds fuel to max and drops car_owner on trade-in
fix: Override decorate to carry fuel_current and owner (see IT-06).
observation: `refresh` rebuilds fuel to max (`Fuel.stampNBT` sets `fuel_current = maxFuel`) and drops `car_owner`. Correct for purchase, wrong for the `decorate` (player→trader) direction, which has no override.
impact: A near-empty fuel can or car valued as full on trade-in.

title: Scoreboard driver appends the title to one shared live line list per board created
fix: Deep-copy scoreboardAddon.getLines() per board so Line state and growth are per player.
observation: `getDriverHandler` hands the **live** `scoreboardAddon.getLines()` list to the driver, whose constructor does `this.lines.add(title)`. Every board creation (each join, each reload) appends another title reference to the one shared list, which grows without bound. The same `Line` objects are also shared by every player, so `Line.index` (the rotating-content cursor) advances once per player per tick — the animated title cycles N× faster with N players and all boards show the same frame
impact: Unbounded list growth; animation speed scales with player count; per-player line state is not per-player

title: Scoreboard updater runs async every tick, touching placeholders and FastBoard
fix: Use timer.start(false) with a configurable interval; keep only pure string formatting off-thread.
observation: `timer.start(true)` schedules `runTaskTimerAsynchronously` at period 1 tick. The task calls `driver.update()` → `Placeholder.convert(player, …)` (gang/user/bank lookups, PlaceholderAPI expansions) and `FastBoard.updateLine/updateTitle` (reflective packet sends). This violates the project's own `feedback_repeating_timer_async` rule and touches non-thread-safe APIs from an async thread, every tick, per player
impact: Race conditions / `ConcurrentModificationException` on domain collections; PlaceholderAPI expansions invoked off-main

title: rerender/switchTo reuse leaves stale clickable and draggable slots
fix: Clear clickableSlots, rightClickSlots, clickableItems and draggableSlots in InventoryHandler.clear() before re-rendering.
observation: `rerender()` and the same-size/same-title `switchTo` reuse path call `current.clear()`, which only clears the Bukkit `Inventory`. `clickableSlots`, `rightClickSlots`, `clickableItems` and `draggableSlots` are never cleared, so a slot the new render leaves **empty** still fires the previous render's click action, and previously-draggable slots stay draggable
impact: Clicking a blank slot triggers a stale action (e.g. an old confirm/deposit button); stale draggable slots let items be inserted/removed

title: InventoryRegistry never unregisters handlers and findByInventory scans everything
fix: Unregister in User.removeInventory and on close, register multi pages through the user, and index handlers by Inventory identity.
tests: FIXED-BY-WS2 0.10.0 CUT, commit 5d6cbefc: InventoryRegistry deleted outright; RemoveAccountListener/KernelConfig no longer construct or clear it; replaced by keystone-inventory's InventoryService/OpenMenuTracker (InventoryHolder-identity-based, no linear scan, auto-untracks on quit via its own MenuListener)
observation: `removeInventory(String)` drops the handler from the user's set but never calls `inventoryRegistry.unregisterInventory`. Multi-inventories additionally register one handler per page at construction while only the head is tracked by the user. `findByInventory` streams every registered handler of every player on every click/drag/close
impact: Registry grows on every inventory open until the player quits; O(total handlers) scan per inventory event

title: Per-user inventory cache hits or misses depending on title/name coincidence
fix: Key the cache by the YAML name consistently and invalidate on open (or drop the cache).
observation: The per-user cache is keyed by `titleRefactor(displayTitle)` compared against the YAML `name`. When they coincide (e.g. `phone.yml`, whose display name resolves to "Phone"), reopening serves the **previously built** handler — stale placeholder values (wallet balance) and stale condition branches. When they differ (`phone_gang`, `gang_info`, …) the cache never hits and a fresh handler is built. The behaviour is therefore accidental and inconsistent between files
impact: Stale GUI contents on some screens only; hard-to-reproduce "my balance doesn't update" reports

title: InventoryOpenByCommandListener return values are inverted and render failures are swallowed
fix: Return true on success and log the exception in the catch.
observation: The success path does `event.setCancelled(true); break;` and then `return false`, so the caller keeps scanning other inventories; the `catch (Exception)` path does `return true` and logs nothing. The two return values are inverted relative to intent
impact: A second inventory bound to the same command would also open; render failures silently swallow the command with no diagnostic

title: Dangling else in MultiInventory.removePage
fix: Add braces so the else-if binds to the outer if.
observation: Dangling `else`: `if (current == 0) if (size > 1) {...} else if (current == size - 1) {...}` — the `else if` binds to the inner `if`, so the "removing the last page" cleanup only runs when `current == 0 && size <= 1 && current == size - 1`
impact: The previous page's next-button is never removed when the tail page is dropped (currently latent — `removePage` has no production caller)

title: Click consumer runs before event.setCancelled
fix: Cancel first, then run the consumer; defer inventory opens by one tick.
observation: The click consumer runs **before** `event.setCancelled(...)`. Consumers routinely call `player.performCommand`, `opener.openInventory` or `AnvilGUI.open` — i.e. a new inventory is opened while the originating `InventoryClickEvent` is still being dispatched, and the cancel is then applied to a stale view
impact: Client/server inventory desync; cursor-item duplication on some client versions

title: Out-of-range Line values throw at open time from a click handler
fix: Validate Line.Vertical/Horizontal at parse time and wrap openInventoryForPlayer in try/catch with a log.
observation: `handler.setItem(usedSlot, …)` performs no bounds check. `InventoryParser.configureSlots` bounds the loop by `factorOfNine(size)` so YAML slots are safe today, but `InventoryUtil.horizontalLine`/`verticalLine` throw `IllegalArgumentException` from `Preconditions` at **open** time when `Configuration.Line.Vertical/Horizontal` is out of range — and `openInventoryForPlayer` has no try/catch
impact: A bad `Line:` value in any inventory YAML throws out of a click handler / interact handler instead of failing at load

title: SPECIAL_INVENTORIES handlers would not cancel clicks (dormant)
fix: Register special inventories in InventoryRegistry or delete the mechanism.
tests: FIXED-BY-WS2 0.10.0 CUT, commit 5d6cbefc: InventoryHandler.SPECIAL_INVENTORIES and its getSpecialInventories() accessor deleted with the class; DebugCommand's /glw debug inv-data special argument (its only reader) deleted too
observation: `SPECIAL_INVENTORIES` is a static map of handlers created with `owner == null`. Such handlers are never registered in `InventoryRegistry`, so `InventoryClickHandler`/`InventoryDragHandler` return early for them and **nothing cancels clicks** — items would be freely removable. No production code path constructs one today (only `removeAllSpecialInventories` is called, from `ReloadPlugin.inventoryReload`)
impact: Dormant item-theft vector if a "special" inventory is ever opened

title: A suspended flow is never cleaned up when the anvil is abandoned
fix: On quit or close during suspend, run cleanup()/onEnd and add a timeout.
observation: If a flow is `suspend()`ed (anvil detour) and the viewer disconnects or the anvil is abandoned without a `resume()`, `current` stays null so `onClose` can never match, `cleanup()` never runs, the host stays registered in Bukkit's `HandlerList`, and `onEnd` (which returns staged items in the trader/banker flows) never fires
impact: Listener + `Player` + session leak; staged items/money never returned

title: VillagerInventory recipe lookup by identity may miss CraftMerchantRecipe
fix: Match by recipe index or result instead of identity.
observation: `recipeToTrade` is an `IdentityHashMap` keyed by the `MerchantRecipe` objects handed to `Merchant.setRecipes`. CraftBukkit converts them to `CraftMerchantRecipe` internally, so `MerchantInventory.getSelectedRecipe()` may return a different instance and `findTradeFor` returns null, silently skipping `onPurchase`
impact: `onPurchase` callbacks never fire on some server versions (currently debug-only usage)

title: Chest hologram removal bypasses HologramService and leaks map entries
fix: Call hologramService.removeHologram(id) in ChestCooldownManager.
observation: `removeChestHologram` calls `hologram.despawn()` directly instead of `hologramService.removeHologram(id)`. The entries stay in `HologramService.holograms` and `hologramsByLocation` forever, and any `createUpdatingHologram` task for them is never cancelled through this path
impact: Map growth proportional to chest-state transitions; `HologramProtectionListener`'s linear scan degrades

title: Holograms vanish after a chunk unload and never respawn
fix: Make the armour stands persistent or respawn them on ChunkLoadEvent/update() when isArmorStandDead.
observation: Armour stands are `setPersistent(false)`, so a chunk unload removes them. `isArmorStandDead` then makes every `update`/`updateLine` a silent no-op and `spawned` stays `true`, so the hologram never respawns. Only a line-count change (which calls `despawn()` + `spawn()`) recovers it
impact: Holograms silently vanish after chunk unload/reload until something changes their line count

title: hologramsByLocation is keyed by the caller's mutable Location
fix: Clone the key on insert and reject a second hologram at the same location.
observation: `hologramsByLocation` is keyed by the caller's `Location` object on insert and by `hologram.getBaseLocation()` (a clone) on removal. This works only because `Location` has value equality — a caller mutating the passed `Location` after the call would orphan the entry. Creating a second hologram at the same location silently overwrites the map entry while leaving the first hologram spawned and in `holograms`
impact: Orphaned armour stands; leaked map entries

title: DriverV1/V2 skip rows that share the title's interval (Wanted never refreshes)
fix: Update every line in the cluster; remove the title-only branch.
tests: WONTFIX/MOVED 0.10.0 WS1 G3 (2026-09-20): DriverV1/DriverV2 (the buggy classes this row describes) were deleted outright along with all of gangland-ui/scoreboard-api when the scoreboard left Gangland for the standalone Plaque plugin (decision WS1-D1(b)) - there is no code left anywhere in this repo matching the row's description. Plaque's own port carries only DriverV3 (already fixed pre-port, per the original docket's own §11 carry-forward table); this row does not apply to Plaque.
observation: When the title's interval matches a row's interval they land in the same cluster and the `if (lines.contains(getTitle())) … else …` branch updates **only** the title, skipping every other line in that cluster. `scoreboard.yml` puts the title and row 3 (`Wanted:`) both at interval 2, so `Wanted` never refreshes under V1/V2. V3 (the default) handles both
impact: Rows silently stop updating when their interval equals the title's, on the two non-default drivers

title: An empty Lines list throws every tick
fix: Guard empty contents in Line and validate scoreboard.yml at load.
observation: `getCurrentContent()` does `contents.get(index)` and `update()` does `% contents.size()` with no empty guard; `ScoreboardAddon.getLines` uses `Objects.requireNonNull(...)` on `Board.<section>`
impact: An empty or missing `Lines:` list in `scoreboard.yml` throws every tick (async task) or NPEs at load

title: Multi.Per_Page is parsed but never read
fix: Use perPage in computeConfigForCreation or remove the key from the three YAMLs.
observation: `Multi.Per_Page` is parsed into `InventoryData.perPage` and never read — `MultiInventoryCreation.computeConfigForCreation` derives per-page purely from `Size` and the static-item count. All three multi files declare `Per_Page: 28` while the effective value is 24 (`phone_gang_search`, `user_stat`, with static items) or 28 (`alliance_stat`)
impact: Dead config key; admin edits have no effect

title: Home_Page head texture key is read but missing from settings.yml
fix: Add Inventory.Multi_Inventory.Home_Page to settings.yml.
observation: `Inventory.Multi_Inventory.Home_Page` is read by `Settings` but the shipped `settings.yml` defines only `Next_Page` and `Previous_Page`
impact: The home-page head texture is not admin-configurable in practice

title: Invalid Action names are swallowed silently (phone.yml RIGHT_CLICK)
fix: Log unknown Action values and fix phone.yml to RIGHT_CLICK_AIR/RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK.
observation: `Open.Event.OnItemClick.Action: RIGHT_CLICK` is not a Bukkit `Action` constant. `parseAction` swallows the `IllegalArgumentException`, leaving the list empty, and `parseActions` then substitutes `RIGHT_CLICK_AIR` + `RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK`. The intended behaviour happens by accident, and any genuine typo is equally silent
impact: Misconfiguration is undetectable; the fallback masks all bad `Action` values

title: phone_bounty.yml slots 21/23/40 have no click handlers
fix: Add OnClick blocks or implement the bounty GUI (see WB-37).
observation: Slots 21 ("Active Bounties"), 23 ("Wanted List") and 40 ("Place Bounty") declare no `OnClick`/`OnRightClick` block, so `processEventItems` returns a non-clickable slot
impact: Three advertised phone features are inert buttons

title: gang_stat.yml has no Slots block, so the GUI is empty
fix: Author the Slots block or remove the button in gang_info. Same as GR-17.
observation: The file has an `Information` block but no `Slots` block; `gang_info` slot 33 opens it
impact: Clicking "Statistics" opens an empty filled chest

title: Anvil output passes through the placeholder engine inside a command string
fix: Escape % in player text before substitution, or convert placeholders before inserting the output.
observation: The anvil `Success.Command` substitutes raw player text into `%gangland_anvil_output%` and then runs `placeholder.convert` over the *result* before `performCommand`. Player-controlled text therefore passes through the placeholder engine as part of a command string
impact: Placeholder injection into an executed command; the command still runs with the player's own permissions, so impact is bounded

title: Raw Sound enum in MultiInventoryNavigation
fix: Use Keystone SoundEffect.
observation: Page-turn feedback uses `player.playSound(loc, XSound.BLOCK_WOODEN_BUTTON_CLICK_ON.get(), …)` with a raw `Sound` enum, contrary to the project rule that all playback goes through Keystone `SoundEffect`
impact: Convention violation; version-drift risk on the `Sound` constant

title: MultiInventory.ID static counter is unsynchronised
fix: Use an AtomicLong.
observation: `MultiInventory.ID` is a mutable static `long` incremented with `++ID` and `MultiInventory.ID = id + 1` from two places, with no synchronisation
impact: Duplicate `NamespacedKey`s under concurrent opens (benign today: pages are renamed immediately afterwards)

title: FilterStore.clearAllForPlayer is never called
fix: Call it on PlayerQuitEvent.
observation: `clearAllForPlayer` has no caller — nothing clears a player's filters on quit or reload
impact: Slow map growth keyed by UUID; a returning player sees their old filter

title: FilterApplier comparator can ClassCastException on mixed types
fix: Compare as strings when classes differ.
observation: The sort comparator does a raw `Comparable.compareTo` guarded only by `b.getClass().isAssignableFrom(a.getClass())`, then falls back to `toString()`
impact: `ClassCastException` on mixed-type projections from a hand-written `FilterAdapter`

title: validateMaterial is a substring match and unknown names kill the whole file
fix: Use exact MaterialType names and XMaterial.matchXMaterial(); skip the slot with a warning.
observation: `validateMaterial` does `Arrays.stream(MaterialType.values()).anyMatch(t -> t.name().contains(value))` — a **substring** test on the YAML value — before falling through to `XMaterial.valueOf(value)`, which throws on unknown names and NPEs on null
impact: A short/odd `Item:` value silently becomes `BLACK_<value>`; an unknown one kills the whole file at load

title: Rebuilt ItemBuilder drops the stack amount
fix: Copy amount (and model data) in InventoryBuilder.
observation: The rebuilt `ItemBuilder` copies type, head, name, lore and the fake enchantment but **not** the stack amount or custom model data from the parsed slot item
impact: `Custom_Model_Data` set on a conditional slot's item survives (it is applied in `SlotItemFactory`) but stack amounts are always 1

title: Open.Permission is enforced but never registered
fix: Register it with PermissionManager.
observation: Only `Information.Permission` is registered with `PermissionManager`; `Open.Permission` (used by `gang_info` and every `UniqueItemHandler`) is enforced but never registered
impact: The permission does not appear in permission dumps; its default is undefined

title: backStack grows when switching between same-size panels
fix: Push only when the panel actually changes.
observation: `switchInternal` pushes onto `backStack` before the reuse check, so repeatedly switching between two panels that share size+title grows the deque unboundedly for the lifetime of the flow
impact: Minor memory growth; `back()` needs many presses to escape

title: Bottom-inventory number-key and offhand swaps are allowed while a GUI is open
fix: Cancel HOTBAR_SWAP and SWAP_WITH_CURSOR for flows that stage player items.
observation: Clicks in the **player's** inventory while a framework GUI is open are only cancelled for `MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY` and `COLLECT_TO_CURSOR`. Number-key swaps, offhand swaps (`F`) and drops from the bottom inventory are allowed
impact: Intended for most GUIs, but flows that stage the player's items (trader sell, barter) rely on their own listeners for this

title: HologramProtectionListener linear scan per interaction
fix: Index armour stands by UUID.
observation: `isHologramArmorStand` linear-scans `holograms.values()` × `lines` on every `PlayerInteractAtEntityEvent` and `PlayerArmorStandManipulateEvent`
impact: O(n·m) per interaction, amplified by issue #13's leak

title: SearchButtonFactory has no callers
fix: Delete it or use it from the YAML views.
observation: The whole class (sort/clear/cycle/text-sink click builders) has no callers — every filter action goes through `/glw filter …` `performCommand` strings in YAML instead
impact: Dead code that duplicates `FilterCommand` logic; the two can drift

title: Multi-event slots resolve non-deterministically
fix: Iterate in a defined order and reject duplicate event blocks.
observation: `processEventItems` iterates `definitionStore.inventoryEvents()` and `playerEvents()` — both plain `HashMap`s — and returns on the first match, so a slot declaring two event blocks gets a non-deterministic winner
impact: Unpredictable behaviour for multi-event slots (none shipped today)

title: Offline cache keyed by Player vs OfflinePlayer: the quit snapshot overwrites the live row after a rejoin
fix: Key both UserManager maps by UUID and evict by UUID on join.
observation: The offline cache is `Map<OfflinePlayer, User<OfflinePlayer>>` but quit inserts with a **`Player`** key (`offlineUserManager.create(player)`), join looks up with a fresh `Player`, and bootstrap inserts with `Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(uuid)`. CraftBukkit's `CraftEntity.equals/hashCode` compare the *entity id*, `CraftOfflinePlayer` compares the UUID, so the key flavours never match: the join-time eviction silently misses and the stale entry survives. `PeriodicalUpdates` writes online users *then* offline users (PeriodicalUpdates.java:108-117), so on the first autosave after a rejoin the quit-time snapshot overwrites the live row for that uuid, rolling back everything earned since rejoining.

title: Every join resets the Vault balance to Initial_Balance until the DB read returns
fix: Set the initial balance only when no user row exists, after the async load, never before it.
observation: `user.getEconomy().setAmount(Settings.getUserInitialBalance())` runs unconditionally on **every** join, before the async DB read. With Vault registered, `EconomyHandler.setAmount` immediately performs `withdrawPlayer(entireBalance)` + `depositPlayer(initial)` on the real Vault account (default `Initial_Balance: 0`), zeroing a returning player's Vault money for the duration of the async round-trip — permanently if the row is missing or the query fails.

title: /glw bank deposit and withdraw accept negative amounts (free cash, negative bank)
fix: Reject amount <= 0 in BankCommand.processMoney and at parse time.
location: BankCommand.java:61-76, used by BankDepositCommand.java:126 and BankWithdrawCommand.java:97
observation: `processMoney` never checks the sign of `amount`. `/glw bank deposit -1000` passes both guards (`-1000 > cash` is false), setting cash to `cash + 1000` and the bank to `bank - 1000` — free cash plus a negative bank balance. `/glw bank withdraw -1000` is the mirror: it moves cash into the bank with **no** daily-cap and **no** tier-cap check, and drives cash negative when the player holds less than the amount.

title: The <amount> <player> forms mint or destroy money for others with no admin gate
fix: Give the target forms a separate admin permission (gangland.command.bank.admin) plus commands.json entries, or remove them.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 c94fceab (#12); manual checklist only - no unit seam for OptionalArgument actions
observation: The `<amount> <player>` target forms credit / debit another player's bank with no fee, no cap check, no daily counter, and nothing taken from the sender — pure money creation/destruction. They are gated only by `gangland.command.bank.deposit` / `.withdraw`, the same node the self-service form uses, and are absent from `commands.json`. Granting a gang rank the deposit permission hands every member an unlimited mint.

title: Death tax withdraw can throw EconomyException inside the death handler
fix: Clamp the deduction to the balance (User.withdraw) and catch EconomyException so changeDeathMessage still runs.
observation: `economy.withdrawAmount(Currency.of(deduct))` has no try/catch. `EconomyException extends PluginException extends RuntimeException` (Keystone `keystone-common/…/exception/PluginException.java:3`), and `withdrawAmount` throws whenever the amount exceeds the balance. A `Death.Money.Formula` that can exceed the balance (e.g. `balance * 0.15 + 500` just above the threshold) throws inside the death handler, so the deduction is skipped **and** `changeDeathMessage` never runs.

title: Death drops mint cash: items are dropped but nothing is debited
fix: Debit the dropped amount from the dead player's balance (or drop only what the tax removed).
observation: On a player death, cash items are dropped (optionally scaled by a fraction of the dead player's balance) but nothing is debited for the drop; the separate death tax is computed from the same balance. Every player death mints currency equal to the rolled variation amount plus the balance bonus.

title: Attribute.MAX_HEALTH on the declared 1.16 floor
fix: Resolve via XAttribute.MAX_HEALTH everywhere (repo-wide pattern; also WB-34, CT-15).
observation: `living.getAttribute(Attribute.MAX_HEALTH)` uses the Attribute constant renamed from `GENERIC_MAX_HEALTH` to `MAX_HEALTH` in the 1.21.3 API. On the declared MC 1.16 floor this resolves to a `NoSuchFieldError` at banker spawn unless the module both compiles against and runs on the newer API.

title: addLevels overshoots maxLevel and a cancelled level-up still consumes XP
fix: Clamp on the resulting level, create a new event per level, subtract XP only when the event is not cancelled.
observation: `addLevels` breaks on `counter >= maxLevel` — the *iteration count*, not the resulting level — so `levelValue` is never clamped to `maxLevel`. It also reuses one `LevelUpEvent` instance for the whole loop, so a single `setCancelled(true)` sticks for every remaining level, and the XP requirement is subtracted before the event is consulted (lines 67 and 120), so a cancelled level-up still consumes the XP.

title: Level meter divides by zero at level 0 (NaN/Infinity, huge string)
fix: Guard requiredExp <= 0 in LevelCommand and Level.getPercentage; guard an empty LEVEL_METER_BAR.
observation: `completeBars = (int) (totalBars * (exp / requiredExp))`. When `experienceCalculation` returns 0 (the default formula `base * level ^ 1.5` yields 0 at level 0, the starting state) the division is `Infinity` or `NaN`, and the loop at line 96 either builds an enormous string on the main thread or renders nothing. `Level.getPercentage()` (Level.java:58) divides by the same value. Line 92 also does `Messages.LEVEL_METER_BAR.toString().charAt(0)`, which throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` if an admin blanks that message.

title: Unchecked (Player) sender casts in bank and level sub-arguments and completers
fix: Guard instanceof Player in completers; rely on user=true for actions.
location: LevelCommand.java:72, BankCommand.java:80, BankBalanceCommand.java:30, BankDepositCommand.java:60, 76 and 142, BankWithdrawCommand.java:53, 69 and 111, BankCreateCommand.java:50
observation: Unchecked `(Player) sender` casts. The parent `Command`s pass `user = true` to the super-constructor, which blocks console at the top level, but every `SubArgument` body repeats the cast with no guard, including the tab-completion lambdas — a console tab-complete would `ClassCastException`.

title: The offline cache is cleared every autosave and never repopulated
fix: Stop clearing the offline cache in the autosave; prune only entries older than N minutes.
observation: `offlineUserManager.clear()` on every autosave tick leaves the offline cache empty for almost the entire uptime, with nothing repopulating it until the next `/glw reload`. Any feature resolving offline users through that bean silently degrades to "not found".

title: Both UserManager beans register suppliers for User and Bank (last wins)
fix: Same fix as CL-23.
observation: Both `UserManager` beans call `initialize()` and both register data suppliers for `User.class` and `Bank.class` on the shared `RepositoryRegistry`; whichever runs last wins and the other manager's contents are invisible to `repositoryRegistry.saveAll()`. Masked today only because `PeriodicalUpdates` writes users/banks with direct table queries.

title: /glw bank create makes an unsaved, tier-less bank
fix: Route through the same creation path as the banker NPC (assign tier, anchor interest, save).
observation: `/glw bank create` produces a `Bank` with `tierId == null` and `lastInterestAt == null` and never calls `bankRepository.save`, while the banker-NPC path assigns the first tier, anchors the interest clock and saves immediately. A chat-created account relies on `resolveTier`'s fallback everywhere and is lost entirely if the server crashes before the next autosave.

title: createBankName and createBankTimer are never cleared on quit
fix: Key by UUID and clear on PlayerQuitEvent.
observation: `createBankName` (`HashMap<User<Player>, …>`) and `createBankTimer` (`HashMap<CommandSender, …>`) are captured in the sub-command constructor and never cleared on quit. A player who starts creation and disconnects leaves strong references to their `User` and `Player` until the 60-second timer fires; if the timer is cancelled another way the entries leak for the plugin's lifetime.

title: perItem * amount overflows int and the cash vanishes
fix: Use long or BigDecimal for the total.
observation: `int total = perItem * stack.getAmount()` overflows for a large `Max` in `money.yml` (any `perItem > 33_554_431` in a full 64-stack), producing a negative total that `GanglandMoneyDepositService.deposit` then silently discards (`amount <= 0`) — the item is already removed, so the money vanishes.

title: Deposit silently discards cash when the user is not cached
fix: Check the user before removing the item entity; notify or log otherwise.
observation: When `userManager.getUser(player)` returns `null` the deposit returns silently *after* the caller has already removed the item entity in all three pickup paths. The cash is destroyed with no message and no log.

title: Holding money cancels every interact (chests, doors, block placement)
fix: Cancel only when the action is the money use itself; skip creative mode.
observation: The listener cancels `PlayerInteractEvent` unconditionally once the held item is money (line 53), so a player holding cash cannot open a chest, use a door, or place a block. It also fires in creative mode with no gamemode guard.

title: Bounty and wanted timers are started async from an async DB task
fix: Start the timers with start(false) from a main-thread task.
observation: Bounty and wanted timers start with `timer.start(true)` (async) from inside an already-async DB task. Per the project's own convention, async timers are only safe for flag flips; if `BountyExecutor` / `WantedExecutor` touch Bukkit entity or world APIs this is an async-API violation. (Executors not inspected — unverified.)

title: UserDataInitEvent is fired async and the scoreboard is created off-thread
fix: Fire the event from a sync task after the async load completes.
tests: STILL OPEN 0.10.0 WS1 G3 (2026-09-20): the scoreboard-side subscriber (PlayerScoreboardListener) was deleted along with the whole scoreboard module, so that specific off-thread scoreboard-creation symptom is gone, but the root cause is untouched - CreateAccountListener.java:105 still constructs `new UserDataInitEvent(true, user)` (async) unconditionally, which still reaches PlayerItemInitBridgeListener.java:20 (org.luckyraven.gangland.listener.bridge) -> PlayerItemInitEvent -> LoadUniqueItem.java:37 off-thread. The docket's fix direction (fire the event from a sync task after the async load completes) is still unaddressed.
observation: `UserDataInitEvent` is fired from the async task with `async = true`. `PlayerScoreboardListener.onUserDataInitialize` constructs a `Scoreboard` and calls `start()` directly, i.e. Bukkit scoreboard API off the main thread.

title: On quit the async clearInventories races the sync save
fix: Run clearInventories synchronously in the same handler.
observation: The LOWEST quit handler schedules an async task calling `user.clearInventories()` — which mutates the shared `InventoryRegistry` — while the HIGHEST handler synchronously removes the user and saves it. Both run in the same tick with no synchronisation on the registry.

title: A banker with a missing world NPEs on every head-track tick
fix: Skip rows whose world is missing (log) and guard getWorld() in findClosestPlayer.
observation: `Bukkit.getWorld(worldName)` can return `null` (world renamed, unloaded, or loaded after the plugin), producing a `Location` with a null world. `BankerNpc.spawn` then calls `npc.spawn(location)` and `BankerManager.findClosestPlayer` calls `location.getWorld().getPlayers()` (BankerManager.java:209) — an unguarded NPE on every head-track tick.

title: Two reloads within two seconds queue two banker spawn passes
fix: Cancel the pending spawn task in onPreClear.
observation: Bankers respawn via `runTaskLater(..., 40L)`. On `/glw reload`, `onPreClear` despawns and `onInitialize` re-schedules; two reloads within two seconds queue two spawn passes. `spawn`'s `existing.isAlive()` guard mitigates but does not close the window while the first batch is still spawning.

title: remove() and init do full-table loads
fix: Delete by the known row; cache loaded rows.
observation: `remove(id)` calls `repository.loadAll()` — a full table read — purely to find the row to delete, and `spawnAllFromRepository` does the same on every init. Repeated full-table I/O on the main thread.

title: bypass_cap skips recordDeposit and the bypass is asymmetric
fix: Record deposits regardless and decide what the bypass covers.
observation: Players with `gangland.bank.bypass_cap` skip `bank.recordDeposit`, so their `deposited_today` never advances; removing the permission later leaves a stale counter. The bypass is also asymmetric — it skips the daily cap but `CAP_EXCEEDED` (line 144) is still enforced.

title: Max_Balance 0 rejects every deposit with no diagnostic
fix: Treat 0 or missing as unlimited and log at load.
observation: The tier-cap check compares against `tier.maxBalance()`. A tier authored with `Max_Balance: 0` (or a missing key, which `parseCurrency` defaults to `"0"`) rejects **every** deposit with `CAP_EXCEEDED` and makes `computeMax` return 0, rendering the amount panel as the "Nothing you can deposit" stub with no diagnostic.

title: snapshot() accrues interest without saving (double pay after a crash)
fix: Save after maintain(), or accrue only inside transactions.
observation: `snapshot()` mutates state (via `maintain` → `accrueInterest`) but never saves.
