The value strongly references the key, defeating weak collection. Entries are only freed by the explicit `active.remove` paths.
impact: If any exit path is missed (e.g. logout without an `InventoryCloseEvent`), the `Player` object and the drop-zone contents leak for the server's lifetime

title: Non-prefixed Weapon_Pool entries are added to both pools
fix: Add only weapon:-prefixed entries to weaponPool.
observation: A `Weapon_Pool` entry that is not `weapon:`-prefixed is added to **both** `weaponNamePool` and `weaponPool`. `resolveGanglandWeapon` then calls `weaponService.getWeapon("IRON_SWORD")` and iterates the whole pool looking for a match that cannot exist.
impact: Wasted lookups plus `canUseWeapons()` returning true for a purely vanilla loadout; the ammo path is skipped so the NPC holds a vanilla item it may not use as intended

title: Item_Pool is parsed but never read
fix: Give civilians the items on spawn or remove the key.
observation: `Item_Pool` is parsed into `CivilianTypeConfig.itemPool()` but there is no reader anywhere in the repo (`grep itemPool()` → no hits), despite `civilians.yml:40-41` documenting the key as functional.
impact: Config key that silently does nothing; server owners will assume items are being given

title: A killed player is re-targeted on return
fix: Clear targetPlayerId in clearCivilianTargets.
observation: `clearCivilianTargets` transitions to IDLE but leaves `targetPlayerId` set; `CivilianIdleBehavior.tick` re-engages any remembered player within `attackRange * 2`.
impact: A player who dies to a hostile civilian is re-targeted the moment they walk back within ~2× attack range, defeating the "clear on death" intent

title: A missing Min_Friend_Discount gives a 100% discount
fix: Default to a sane value (e.g. 0.5) and clamp priceMultiplier.
observation: `Min_Friend_Discount` defaults to `0.0` when the key is missing, and `MoodService.priceMultiplier` becomes `1 - mood` — a 100% discount at max mood.
impact: A trait file missing one key hands out free items once a player has tipped enough

title: findClosestPlayer NPEs when the trader's world is missing
fix: Guard getWorld() and skip the trader.
observation: `findClosestPlayer` calls `location.getWorld().getPlayers()` with no null check; `TraderRepository.doLoadAll:53-54` can produce a `Location` with a null world when `Bukkit.getWorld(name)` misses.
impact: NPE inside the 2-tick head-track task, which then stops running for every trader

title: requireNonNull on nullable worlds
fix: Guard and skip the cycle.
observation: `Objects.requireNonNull(npcLoc.getWorld())` / `Objects.requireNonNull(world)` on values Bukkit declares nullable.
impact: NPE aborts the whole proximity-spawner cycle or the NPC tick (the tick is caught and the NPC is removed; the spawner loop is not)

title: Attribute.MAX_HEALTH vs the 1.16 floor
fix: Same as US-07.
observation: Both use `Attribute.MAX_HEALTH`, the 1.21.3+ registry name, while `CLAUDE.md` states the MC floor is 1.16.
impact: If the modules are compiled against a newer Spigot API than the runtime, health application throws `NoSuchFieldError` on older servers

title: ECONOMY_ERROR on tip only plays a sound
fix: Send a message.
observation: `TipResult.ECONOMY_ERROR` only plays a sound; no message is sent.
impact: Silent failure — the player sees nothing after clicking TIP

title: Shop price is not rounded to 2 dp
fix: setScale(2, HALF_UP).
observation: `price.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(multiplier))` is never scaled or rounded; the charged amount can carry a long decimal tail (the sell/barter valuators do scale to 2 dp).
impact: Charged price differs from the formatted price shown; inconsistent with the sell side

title: MAX_MODE_CYCLE is hard-coded
fix: Use ShopUiSettings.getMaxModeMultiplier().
observation: `MAX_MODE_CYCLE = 8` is hard-coded, ignoring `ShopUiSettings.getMaxModeMultiplier()` which `PriceEditorView.java:268` does honour.
impact: `Trader.Max_Mode_Multiplier` only affects half the UI it claims to govern

title: Mood map is never persisted or pruned
fix: Prune on quit and document the reset.
observation: Mood is a plain in-memory map, never persisted and never pruned when a player logs out.
impact: All trader relationships reset on restart (a design decision, but undocumented in `trader_traits.yml`); the map grows with the unique-player set

title: remove() does a full table load
fix: Delete by the known row.
observation: `remove()` calls `repository.loadAll()` and streams it to find the row to delete instead of holding the already-known `TraderData`.
impact: Depending on `AbstractRepository` caching this may re-read the whole table on every removal; also fails to delete if the row was never flushed

title: A killed trader drops its equipment
fix: Clear drops and XP in TraderDamageListener like CivilianDeathListener.
observation: Nothing suppresses a killed trader's death drops or XP (contrast `CivilianDeathListener` which clears both). A killable trader (`stubborn`) is a PLAYER-type Citizens NPC.
impact: Killing a trader may drop its equipment; the NPC's `PlayerDeathEvent` path is not neutralised

title: A price edit may mutate the shared ItemStack (unverified)
fix: Deep-copy the ItemStacks in deepCopySell.
observation: `new ItemBuilder(existing).addTag(...).build()` — if `ItemBuilder` mutates the wrapped stack in place, the tag lands on the shared `ItemStack` instance the original (non-copied) definition still references, so a CANCEL in the price editor would not undo it. `ShopAdminFlow.deepCopySell` copies the *list* but not the individual `ItemStack`s.
impact: Price edits could leak into the live definition even when cancelled

title: Concurrent admin saves are last-writer-wins
fix: Merge on save or lock the shop while editing.
observation: `save` is not synchronized and `FileHandler.save()` is a plain write. Two admins ending edit flows on the same shop in the same tick sequence both write full files from their own working copies.
impact: Last-writer-wins; the first admin's changes vanish with no warning

title: commands.json lacks a "civilian" root entry
fix: Add it.
observation: Root entry `"civilian"` is absent (only `civilian_help`), while `shop` and `trader` both have root entries.
impact: Help listing for `/glw civilian` has no description entry

title: Behaviour.Enabled false also disables proximity spawning
fix: Split the two timers behind separate settings.
observation: `Civilians.Behaviour.Enabled: false` skips starting **both** timers, including the proximity spawner.
impact: Disabling "AI" silently also disables all automatic civilian spawning — not what the comment in `settings.yml:515` implies

title: Group keys include nanoTime
fix: Use a stable id.
observation: `registerGroup` keys the map by `groupId + "_" + System.nanoTime()`, so the group map is append-only until `tickAll` prunes empties.
impact: Fine in practice, but the key is not addressable — `getActiveGroups()` streams are the only lookup path

title: ignoreCancelled on a non-Cancellable event
fix: Remove the flag.
observation: `ignoreCancelled = true` on `CivilianDeathEvent`, which does not implement `Cancellable`.
impact: No functional effect; misleading

title: A capture completes into a disbanded gang's id with no event and no cleanup
fix: Check newOwner != null before setOwnerGangId/persist; on null cancel the contest and fire TurfCaptureFailedEvent.
observation: `turf.setOwnerGangId(newOwnerId)` + `turfs.persist(turf)` run **before** the `newOwner != null` check, so a capture completing against a disbanded gang writes a dangling owner id and fires no `TurfCapturedEvent` — boss bars, defenders and the engaged Quartermaster are never cleaned up until the income task auto-releases the turf.

title: reinforced_defense and garrison_discount buffs are purchasable but do nothing
fix: Apply CAPTURE_DEFENSE_BONUS in the CaptureService weighting and GARRISON_DISCOUNT in the garrison price.
observation: `EffectType.CAPTURE_DEFENSE_BONUS` and `GARRISON_DISCOUNT` have **no consumer anywhere in the repo** (`effectiveMultiplier` is called only by `TurfIncomeDistributor:70` with `INCOME_MULTIPLIER`). `reinforced_defense` (8000) and `garrison_discount` (2500) in `turf_powerups.yml` are purchasable and do nothing.

title: Turf delete leaves contests, boss bars, child rows and NPCs behind
fix: In TurfManager.delete cancel the contest, fire the failed event, delete child rows and despawn the Quartermaster.
observation: `delete` does not cancel an in-flight contest, fire `TurfCaptureFailedEvent`, clear boss bars, delete `turf_garrison` / `turf_active_buff` / `turf_powerup_npc` rows, or despawn the Quartermaster. `TurfBossBarListener.barsByTurf` keeps the entry forever (`refreshProgress` just `continue`s).

title: Admin setowner leaves bars, defenders and the NPC in contest state
fix: Fire TurfCaptureFailedEvent(CANCELLED) from TurfSetOwnerCommand.
observation: Admin ownership change resets the runtime state but fires no `TurfCaptureFailedEvent`, so capture boss bars persist, defenders are not recalled and the Quartermaster stays in COMBAT against the (now irrelevant) challenger.

title: A deleted highest id is reused, so a new turf inherits orphaned rows
fix: Delete child rows on turf delete (TF-03) and never reuse ids (persist nextId or use autoincrement).
observation: `nextId` is seeded to `max(existingId)+1`, so deleting the highest-id turf and restarting **re-uses that id**; the new turf then inherits the deleted turf's orphaned garrison stock, active buffs and Quartermaster row (all keyed by `turf_id` with no FK).

title: TurfLocationTracker.onQuit is never registered, so the cache grows forever
fix: Annotate with @ListenerHandler (drop the @Bean) or register the listener explicitly.
observation: The class implements `Listener` and declares `onQuit`, but has no `@ListenerHandler` and is created as a `@Bean`; Keystone registers only `@ListenerHandler` classes (`ListenerService:151`), so the handler never fires and `playerTurfCache` grows unbounded for the server's lifetime.

title: No turf bean implements BeanLifecycle and the stop() methods have no callers
fix: Implement BeanLifecycle on the TurfConfig beans: stop tasks in onPreClear, restart in onInitialize.
observation: No turf bean implements `BeanLifecycle`. `TurfLocationTracker.stop`, `TurfIncomeDistributor.stop`, `GangPresenceTracker.stop`, `TurfContributionTickTask.stop`, `ActiveBuffManager.shutdown` and `TurfDefenderDeployer.stop` have **zero callers**. A `/glw reload` therefore re-reads no `Turf.*` setting and cancels no task.

title: The boss bar refresh task has no cancel path
fix: Store the task and cancel it in onShutdown.
observation: The 1-Hz refresh task is scheduled inside the constructor with no stored handle and no cancel path.

title: The inactivity task's initial delay equals its 24h period
fix: Use a short initial delay.
observation: The inactivity-release task is scheduled with an initial delay equal to its 24 h period, so a server restarted daily never runs `InactivityReleaseTask`.

title: Auto-release fires no TurfOwnerChangedEvent
fix: Fire the event and play the owner-cleared sound.
observation: Auto-release nulls the owner and persists, but fires no `TurfOwnerChangedEvent` — the presence boss bar stays stale and the "owner cleared" sound never plays, contradicting `TurfSoundContract.playOwnerCleared`'s javadoc. Defenders/Quartermaster are not touched.

title: "Push CLAIM to zero and steal" is not implemented; the exclude parameter is dead
fix: Implement the CLAIM<=0 branch (exclude the failed challenger) or delete the dead code and fix the settings.yml comments.
observation: `dominantGang`'s `exclude` parameter is dead (both call sites pass `null`) and the CLAIM≤0 branch (`:360-364`) is documented as unreachable — the "push Phase 1 to zero and steal the contest" reward described in `CapturePhase`'s javadoc and in `settings.yml`'s comment (lines 724-728) is **not implemented**.

title: Abandon_Grace_Seconds is ignored on owned turfs
fix: Cancel the contest after the grace window using lastChallengerSeenAt.
observation: `Abandon_Grace_Seconds` is never consulted on the owned-turf path; abandonment is handled by a `-1` decay instead, so an emptied contest lingers for up to `Duration_Seconds` rather than the configured grace. `lastChallengerSeenAt` is written but never read there.

title: Unboxing a @Nullable challenger id
fix: Null-check before unboxing.
observation: `int newOwnerId = state.getChallengerGangId();` auto-unboxes a `@Nullable Integer`. Currently unreachable with a null challenger, but a single new completion path would turn it into an NPE inside a 1-Hz task.

title: TurfRepository hard casts may ClassCastException on MySQL
fix: Use Number casts like the sibling repositories.
observation: Hard casts `(int) result[v++]` / `(long) result[v]` where the sibling repositories use `((Number) x).intValue()`. If the SQLite/MySQL backend hands back a `Long` for an INTEGER column, turf loading dies with a `ClassCastException`.

title: income_amount is stored as Double (BigDecimal loss)
fix: Store as a string or DECIMAL column.
observation: `income_amount` is persisted as a SQL `Double` while `Turf.incomeAmount` is a `BigDecimal` — lossy round-trip on every restart.

title: A hardcoded y < 0 || y > 319 filter excludes deep players
fix: Remove the Y filter; the region is Y-agnostic.
observation: Hardcoded `if (y < 0 || y > 319) continue;` excludes players below y=0 in 1.18+ worlds from capture/defence bonuses, contradicting `CuboidRegion`'s Y-agnostic containment.

title: PER_DEFENDER_COST is hard-coded
fix: Move it to turf_powerups.yml and apply GARRISON_DISCOUNT.
observation: `PER_DEFENDER_COST = BigDecimal.valueOf(1500)` is hardcoded (the class javadoc admits it should be in `turf_powerups.yml`), and the `GARRISON_DISCOUNT` buff that is supposed to modify it is never applied.

title: The buff catalogue shows only 9 entries
fix: Paginate.
observation: Only slots 9-17 render buffs, so a catalogue with more than 9 entries silently hides the rest with no pagination.

title: The powerup panel does not re-validate ownership on click
fix: Re-check the turf owner/ally in attemptBuy.
observation: The session caches the `Turf` and gangs at open time and nothing re-validates ownership on click, so a capture that lands while the panel is open lets the previous owner (or an ally) pay for a buff/defender on the enemy's turf.

title: The whole garrison is consumed on the first capture start
fix: Deploy incrementally and refund on an instant cancel; spawn around the fight, not one column.
observation: The whole garrison stock is consumed by the first `TurfCaptureStartEvent`; a contest that starts and cancels in one tick burns everything. All defenders also spawn at one surface column derived from `getHighestBlockYAt`, which can be a roof or far from the fight.

title: No region size validation; perimeter particles every second
fix: Validate min/max size and throttle particles.
observation: No minimum/maximum region size is validated at creation, and `/glw turf show` emits particles along the entire perimeter at 0.5-block steps every second per viewer — a large turf is a visible TPS cost.

title: 59 TURF_* keys are missing from message_es
fix: Covered by CM-15.
observation: None of the 59 `TURF_*` message paths present in `message_en.yml` exist in the Spanish file (verified by path diff) — the whole feature is untranslated for that locale.

title: Hardcoded English and "$" in the turf views
fix: Route through TurfMessageContract and Settings.getMoneySymbol().
observation: User-facing strings are hardcoded English (and `$` is hardcoded instead of `Settings.getMoneySymbol()`), bypassing the `TurfMessageContract` convention used everywhere else in the feature.

title: One-directional ally checks
fix: Use a symmetric helper (either side).
observation: Ally checks use a single direction (`other.isAlly(ownerGang)` / `attackerGang.isAlly(ownerGang)`); if `GangAlliance` records are not written on both gangs, defender-folding and friendly-fire protection are asymmetric.

title: Disbanding a gang does not release its turfs
fix: Release turfs (fire owner-changed) in GangManager.remove or a gang-delete listener.
observation: Disbanding a gang does not release its turfs; cleanup only happens on the 10-minute income pass or the daily inactivity sweep. In between, `findById` returns null and a running contest can still complete into the dead id (see #1).

title: A third gang on an owned turf is ignored (intentional per javadoc)
fix: No change; documented.
observation: On an owned turf only the registered challenger gang's members count; members of any other gang inside are ignored entirely (they neither help nor hinder and cannot start their own contest). Intentional per the javadoc, but it means a rival gang can body-block nothing.

title: COOLDOWN is not persisted, so a turf reads IDLE after restart
fix: Derive COOLDOWN from lastCaptureTimestamp on load.
observation: After a restart a turf still inside its cooldown window reports `IDLE`, because the COOLDOWN enum value is not persisted while `lastCaptureTimestamp` is.

title: Reason.CANCELLED is never fired
fix: Fire it from delete and setowner (TF-03/04).
observation: Declared but never fired anywhere.

title: A cross-world corner wipes both corners; ID_TAKEN is never sent
fix: Reject the corner instead and add a duplicate-name check.
observation: A cross-world corner wipes both corners, so `TURF_CREATE_FAIL_CROSS_WORLD` is effectively unreachable through the wand and `/glw turf pos1|pos2` paths. `TURF_CREATE_FAIL_ID_TAKEN` is never sent at all (no duplicate-name check).

title: Two admin permission namespaces
fix: Unify on gangland.command.turf.*.
observation: The wand uses `gangland.turf.admin` while every subcommand uses `gangland.command.turf.<sub>` — two disjoint namespaces for the same admin surface.

title: /glw turf buff activates for free (staff tool)
fix: Document it; optionally charge.
observation: `/glw turf buff <id>` activates any catalogue buff **free of charge** on the selected turf. Intentional (staff tool) but the only gate is the `gangland.command.turf.buff` permission.

title: prune deletes one row per expired buff on the main thread
fix: Batch the deletes.
observation: `prune` issues one synchronous `repository.delete` per expired buff from a 1-Hz main-thread task.

title: remove() loads the whole table
fix: Delete by id.
observation: `remove(turfId)` calls `repository.loadAll()` (a full table read) to find one row to delete.

title: getTurfsInWorld returns the live list
fix: Return an unmodifiable copy.
observation: `getTurfsInWorld` returns the live `ArrayList` (not a copy) held inside a `ConcurrentHashMap`, and `delete` mutates it. Safe today only because everything runs on the main thread.

title: Linear scan per damage event in findOwningTurfId
fix: Index defenders by entity UUID.
observation: Linear scan over every group × defender on **every** `EntityDamageByEntityEvent` and `WeaponRaytraceImpactEvent`.

title: turf_npcs.yml is never re-read
fix: Reload in onInitialize (TF-07).
observation: `load()` is only called from the constructor, so `turf_npcs.yml` is never re-read; `TurfDefenderConfig` / `TurfPowerupSettings` are boot-time snapshots.

title: Income has no cap and no online requirement
fix: Cap the multiplier product; optional online requirement.
observation: Income is paid with no online-member requirement, no upkeep, and no cap on the aggregated `INCOME_MULTIPLIER` product (stacking is multiplicative and unbounded).

title: The powerup NPC display name is always null
fix: Pass the configured name.
observation: Always passes `null` for the display name, so `TurfPowerupData.display_name` is always null and the panel title falls back to the literal `"Quartermaster"`.

title: There is no /glw turf rename
fix: Add the command.
observation: No `/glw turf rename` command exists; the setter has no caller, so a turf's name is fixed at creation.

title: Turf delete does not cancel an in-flight contest: boss bars and guards linger (TF-03 residual)
fix: Route delete through the W0-A ownership pipeline: TurfDeleteCommand calls TurfOwnership.cancelContest(turf, DELETED) before turfs.delete, which fires TurfCaptureFailedEvent so TurfBossBarListener and GarrisonDeployListener clean up. Covering tests: extend TurfDeleteCommandTest (contest cancelled, failed event fired once), NEW TurfOwnershipTest. [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W0-A of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] TurfDeleteCommand removes the turf, garrison, buff and Quartermaster rows (L63-66) but never cancels a contest in flight. TurfManager.delete drops the runtime state (L124) without firing TurfCaptureFailedEvent, so TurfBossBarListener.refreshProgress just skips the vanished state (its bars stay in barsByTurf) and the defenders deployed for the contest are only recalled by the capture events (GarrisonDeployListener.onFailed), so they persist until their safety lifespan runs out. Residual of TF-03, which cleaned the child rows but not the contest.

title: TurfModuleConfig.garrisonManager and turfManager call initialize() and the LIFECYCLE convention calls it again
fix: W0-B: drop the explicit initialize() call from both @Bean methods and leave it to the BeanFactory convention pass, the same fix GI-82 applied to activeBuffManager. Covering tests: extend TurfModuleConfigTest (garrisonManager and turfManager do not self-initialize: the repository is loaded once). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W0-B of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
location: gangland-turf turf/TurfModuleConfig.java:88-94,111-116 (explicit calls L92, L114); turf/manager/TurfManager.java:43; turf/powerups/GarrisonManager.java:24; Keystone keystone-bean BeanFactory.java:713-741 (findInitializeMethod)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] Both @Bean methods call manager.initialize() before returning the bean, and Keystone's BeanFactory convention pass also calls any public no-arg void initialize() by name during LIFECYCLE, so each repository is loaded twice (TurfManager.initialize clears its maps and runtime state and reloads; GarrisonManager.initialize reloads and re-registers the data supplier). Harmless today because both are idempotent, but it is the same class of double init as GI-82 (fixed for ActiveBuffManager, and documented at TurfModuleConfig.java:80).

title: TurfPowerupManager.remove never purges the pending chunk-load queue
fix: W0-B: remove() also drops the turf's entries from the pending queue (and looks the row up by turf id instead of loadAll().stream()). Covering tests: extend TurfPowerupManagerTest (pending entry purged on remove, a later chunk load spawns nothing). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W0-B of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] remove() destroys the live NPC and deletes the repository row but leaves a queued TurfPowerupData in pending (L41, filled at L173 when the anchor chunk is not loaded at boot). onChunkLoaded (L146-152) then spawns a Quartermaster for the deleted turf and registers it in byTurfId. Split out of TF-33's evidence; TF-33 keeps the full-table read per removal.

title: TurfVisualization sends about 4,200 particles per second per viewer on a 256 x 256 turf, with no clipping
fix: W3-V: clip TurfVisualization to a 40-block window around the viewer and use an adaptive step so the per-refresh point count is bounded whatever the turf size; the /glw map border outline reuses it. Covering tests: NEW TurfVisualizationClipTest (bounded point count for a 512 x 512 turf). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W3-V of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] renderEdges draws two full rectangles (top and bottom of a +-10 block Y band) at STEP 0.5 plus four pillars once per REFRESH_TICKS (20 ticks), one spawnParticle call per point and no clipping to the viewer's distance. For a 256 x 256 turf that is 2 x 2,048 rectangle points + 4 x 41 pillar points, about 4,260 calls per second per viewer for the whole show duration, built on the main thread. Derived from the constants; not measured on a client.

title: Member.contribution mixes bank share and turf points, so turf farming claims bank money on disband
fix: W2-P1: delete the turf contribution tick and listener (TF-16) so Member.contribution is bank share only, reset stored mixed values to 0 on the first 0.14.0 boot (owner decision D15, PLAN recommends B), and let a disband with all-zero contributions split the vault equally. Covering tests: GangDeleteCommandTest payout with all-zero contributions = equal split; migration test (mixed values reset to 0). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W2-P1 of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] One field holds two units. GangDepositCommand adds the bank share (amount / Gang_Contribution_Rate) to Member.contribution, and the turf module adds turf points to the same field through increaseContribution from the 1 Hz presence tick (TurfContributionTickTask L97) and the capture listener (TurfContributionListener L68). GangDeleteCommand.payouts then splits the whole vault pro rata on that single number, so a member who farms turf points takes a share of other members' deposits on disband.

title: gangland.turf.capture, contribute and upgrade have no production consumer, so any recruit spends the gang bank at the Quartermaster
fix: W2-Q wires gangland.turf.upgrade through GangPermissions.allows on every Quartermaster spend (officer rank carries it), re-validated on each click; W2-P1 deletes the capture and contribute nodes and the RankPermissionApplierTest fixtures that name them. Covering tests: purchase re-validation with a recording fake; an officer cannot exceed the guard reserve cap; a recruit cannot spend the bank. [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W2-Q (upgrade wired) and W2-P1 (fixtures deleted) of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
tests: RankPermissionApplierTest (fixtures name gangland.turf.capture/contribute/upgrade; replace with the live nodes when fixed)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] The three rank permission strings appear in no production code (only as RankPermissionApplierTest fixtures), and the turf module contains no rank or permission check other than the admin ones. Both Quartermaster spend paths call gang.getEconomy().withdrawAmount after only checking that the viewer has a gang, so the lowest rank can empty the bank on buffs or guards.

title: GarrisonDeployListener consumes the garrison stock before deploy no-ops without Citizens
fix: W3-B: consume the stock only after defenders actually spawned and refund whatever did not spawn; with Citizens absent do nothing and burn nothing. Covering tests: TurfDefenderDeployerTest (no consume without Citizens; refund on a failed spawn), GarrisonManagerTest (refund). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W3-B of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] onCaptureStart calls garrisons.consume (L70) and then defenders.deploy (L73). deploy returns early when NpcSupport.available() is false (L89) and skips any spawnCivilian that returns null (L97-101), so the guards the owner bought are consumed and never appear on a Citizens-less server or after a failed spawn. The comment at TurfDefenderDeployer L86-88 records the stock staying consumed as the intended contract.

title: Guard squads key on (faction, target) with no turf scope, so two turfs' guards can recruit each other
fix: W3-A: add a scope (the turf id) to SquadKey and route alertFaction, recruit and drainPendingRecruits through a public CivilianService.squadFor(npc, target, scope) so squads never span turfs; the default scope stays empty so the cops and civilian default path is unchanged. Covering tests: two turfs' guards never share a squad; two attackers on one turf make one CONTACT per target squad; existing CivilianServiceSquadTest stays green. [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W3-A of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] SquadKey is (faction, targetId) (L351) and the turf defender type carries Faction: turf_defender (civilians.yml L238), so every turf's guards share one squad per attacker. recruit() (L260) then pulls every hostile same-faction NPC within its Alert_Range (default 16) or the 24-block shout range with no turf check, so guards of neighbouring turfs can be pulled onto an attacker who is only raiding one of them. Key shape confirmed in code; cross-turf recruitment depends on turf layout and was not reproduced live.

title: One rival alt standing inside an owned turf blocks every capture start (exactly one challenger rule)
fix: W2-R: replace the exactly-one-challenger rule with strict plurality: the bar starts when one gang has more members inside than the owners plus allies and more than any other single gang, so a lone third-gang member no longer blocks. Covering tests: alt-blocker red then green in the plurality tables (sum and largest-single cases); re-scope CaptureServiceStartAndCompleteTest.ownedTurf_multipleChallengerGangsBlockStart, which pins only the 1-vs-1 tie. [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W2-R of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
tests: CaptureServiceStartAndCompleteTest.ownedTurf_multipleChallengerGangsBlockStart (pins the 1-vs-1 tie only; re-scope to plurality when fixed)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] classify() folds the owner and its allies into defenders and every other in-turf player who has a gang into challengersByGang; the owned-turf start requires defenders == 0 and challengersByGang.size() == 1 (L209), so one member of any third gang (an alt, a passer-by) inside the turf blocks every start for as long as he stays. Players with no gang are skipped and do not block. The comment at L207-208 presents this as intended bystander behaviour.

title: Defending your own turf raises your wanted level (no defender exemption exists)
fix: Optional W4-H (owner decision D10): add a default exemptsKill(Player, Entity) to core WantedKillTracker (forwarded by WantedKillTrackers), consult it in EntityDamageListener.handlePlayerKills, and implement it in cops KillComboWantedTracker from turf contest state so kills made defending your own turf during a contest do not raise wanted; attacker and outside kills unchanged. Covering tests: WantedKillTrackersTest, KillComboWantedTrackerTest (defender inside exempt; attacker not; outside not; no contest not). [found by gang-turf planning wave 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W4-H (optional) of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, gang-turf planning wave census + review] Design gap, not a regression. handlePlayerKills counts any real-player kill toward the killer's wanted level (recordKill L146 or handleWanted L148) and neither EntityDamageListener nor WantedKillTracker knows about turfs or contests, so the owner who kills an attacker on their own turf mid-contest is wanted for it. Whether that is wanted is an owner decision (D10).

title: The configured explosion damage is used as the explosion radius (50-block rockets)
fix: Add a dedicated Explosion_Radius (default per projectile type) for the radius and keep Explosion_Damage for damage.
observation: `explosionRadius = weapon.getDamageData().getExplosionDamage()` — the configured **damage** is used as the explosion **radius**. `rocket_launcher.yml` has `Explosion_Damage: 50`, producing a 50-block-radius AOE.
impact: Rocket kills everything within 50 blocks; `getNearbyEntities` over a 100-block cube every rocket

title: Rocket damage is hard-coded 20 * falloff
fix: Use weapon.getDamageData().getExplosionDamage() in SteppedProjectileTask.
observation: Explosion damage is hardcoded `20 * (1 - distance/radius)`; the configured `Explosion_Damage` is never used as damage.
impact: Rocket damage is unconfigurable and unrelated to YAML

title: Biological weapons deal no health damage
fix: Let the impact handler fall through to the damage pipeline (or apply the damage inside the handler).
observation: The `impactHandler` applies potion effects only. `WeaponRaytracer.handleEntityImpact:428-438` returns before the default damage pipeline whenever an impact handler is present, so the computed `Base_Damage * level` is fired in the event but never dealt.
impact: Biological weapons deal zero health damage

title: Grenades damage twice (createExplosion plus the manual loop)
fix: Create the explosion without entity damage and keep only the manual loop.
observation: `world.createExplosion(..., player)` damages living entities, then the loop below damages the same entities again with `Explosion_Damage`.
impact: Grenades deal roughly double the configured damage

title: A non-sneaking left click on scope-less weapons is consumed by the scope branch
fix: validateScope must return false when scopeData == null.
observation: `validateScope` stays `true` when `scopeData == null`, so the scope branch consumes and `return`s on **every** non-sneaking left click for weapons with no `Scope:` section — including all melee weapons.
impact: Left-click-air melee only works while sneaking; entity swings still work via `EntityDamageByEntityEvent`

title: Every getWeapon(type) with a null UUID mints a registry entry and a DB row
fix: Return the template (or a transient clone) for converters, refreshers and messages; mint only on an actual give; prune unowned rows in the cleanup.
observation: Every `getWeapon(type)` call with a null UUID mints a fresh `Weapon` + random UUID and puts it in the registry. Converters, refreshers, `/glw weapon give` and every throwable death message hit this path.
impact: Unbounded growth of `WeaponService.weapons` and of the `weapon` DB table (one row per item ever created); autosave cost grows without bound

title: getModifiersData() NPEs for weapons without a Modifiers section
fix: Create an empty ModifiersData by default in the parser.
observation: `weapon.getModifiersData()` is dereferenced without a null check; `ModifiersData` is only created when a `Modifiers:` YAML section exists (`ModifiersSectionParser.java:42-47`).
impact: NPE on the first block/entity hit for any admin-authored weapon lacking `Modifiers:`; all 22 shipped files happen to have one

title: Spread reset compares ticks to milliseconds, so spread never accumulates
fix: Convert resetTime ticks to ms (x50) before comparing.
observation: `spreadData.getResetTime()` is authored in ticks (`Time: 5`) but compared against a millisecond delta.
impact: Spread resets on virtually every shot; `Change.Base`/`Bounds` accumulation never takes effect

title: Per-weapon state maps are never cleared on quit, death or shutdown
fix: Clear every WeaponInteract map for the player's weapons on quit and in onShutdown; cancel the tasks.
observation: `pressLockUntilTick`, `pressHoldState`, `releaseCallbacks`, `autoTasks`, `activeTasks`, `meleeCooldowns`, `lastMeleeSwingMs` are keyed by weapon UUID and only cleared by `onWeaponHeld` for the previous slot. No `PlayerQuitEvent`, death or shutdown cleanup.
impact: Map growth over server uptime; charge/fire tasks survive a quit and keep touching a stale `Player`

title: Reload timers survive quit and shutdown; the reloading flag can stick
fix: Cancel reload timers on quit, death and shutdown and always reset reloading.
observation: No reload timer is cancelled on `PlayerQuitEvent`, on death outside a timer step, or on plugin shutdown. `WeaponReloadListener.onPlayerQuit` only removes a marker.
impact: Reload timers keep a `Player` reference and write to the inventory after quit; `reloading` can stay true forever if the timer is null when `stopReloading` is called

title: Division by zero for Capacity 0 or num-0
fix: Validate > 0 at parse time.
observation: `leftToInsert / ammunitionData.getRestore()` and `numberOfAmmunition / amount` with no zero guard.
impact: `ArithmeticException` for `Capacity: 0` or `Type: num-0`

title: A cancelled shot refunds 1 instead of Consumed_Amount
fix: Refund projectileData.getConsumed().
observation: On a cancelled `WeaponShootEvent` the refund is a fixed `addAmmunition(1)`, while `GunWeapon.consumeShot` subtracted `projectileData.getConsumed()`.
impact: Magazine drift when `Consumed_Amount != 1`

title: Consumed_Amount defaults to 0, giving an infinite magazine
fix: Default to 1.
observation: `Consumed_Amount` defaults to `0` (`min(0).orDefault(0)`), and `GunWeapon.consumeShot` subtracts that value.
impact: A gun YAML omitting `Consumed_Amount` has an infinite magazine; all shipped files set it to 1

title: Biological ammo is never written to NBT; melee and throwable never consume
fix: Call updateWeaponData after consumeShot in BiologicalAction; decide and implement ammo for melee/throwable across all five types.
observation: `consumeShot()` mutates only the in-memory object with no `updateWeaponData`/`updateWeapon`, so the `ammo-left` NBT is never rewritten; melee and throwable never call `consumeShot` at all.
impact: Biological ammo is restored on the next interaction; melee/throwable "ammunition" is decorative

title: An empty Effects_Per_Level gives index -1
fix: Validate at parse time and guard in the action.
observation: `effectsPerLevel.get(min(level, size) - 1)` yields index `-1` when `Effects_Per_Level` is empty.
impact: `IndexOutOfBoundsException` on release

title: ReloadType.amount is shared mutable enum state
fix: Store the amount on the weapon's AmmunitionData, not the enum.
observation: `amount` is a mutable field on the enum constant, shared by every weapon using that reload type. It is read at weapon-construction time, so today's configs work, but any later read of `ReloadType.NUM.getAmount()` returns whichever file loaded last.
impact: Fragile shared global state; two `num-N` weapons with different N would collide on any later read

title: WITHDRAWN: Consume_Rate is live (IncendiaryWeapon.consumeShot)
fix: No change.
observation: WITHDRAWN: `Consume_Rate` *is* read — `IncendiaryWeapon.consumeShot()` (`IncendiaryWeapon.java:33-37`) overrides the base method and subtracts `incendiaryData.getConsumeRate()`, so the key is live and `IncendiaryAction.sprayFire:97` consumes `Consume_Rate` per fire tick (gated on `tracksAmmo`).
impact: Dead config key; the documented knob has no effect

title: WeaponEntityDamageEvent and WeaponKillEntityEvent are never fired
fix: Fire them from the damage pipeline (CarDamageListener depends on one) or delete them.
observation: Neither event is ever fired anywhere in the repo. `CarDamageListener.onWeaponEntityDamage` (`:166`) is bound to one of them.
impact: Dead code path; the vehicle handler is unreachable

title: AP damage is dealt without a damager (no kill credit)
fix: Use target.damage(amount, player).
observation: The armor-piercing half is applied via `target.damage(pierceDmg)` with no damager.
impact: No kill credit, no `getKiller()`, no death message for AP finishing blows

title: Grenade self-damage is unattributed and double-counted
fix: Skip the manual self-damage or attribute it.
observation: Thrower self-damage is `player.damage(totalDmg)` with no damager, on top of the vanilla explosion self-damage.
impact: Suicide by own grenade is unattributed and double-counted

title: pendingKillerWeapon leaks for survivors
fix: Expire entries after N ticks.
observation: `pendingKillerWeapon` is only drained by `PlayerDeathListener`; entries for entities that survive the blast are never removed.
impact: Slow map leak keyed by every entity ever caught in a blast

title: setInvulnerable(false) permanently clears the target's flag
fix: Do not touch invulnerability; skip invulnerable targets.
observation: `living.setInvulnerable(false)` permanently clears the flag on the target.
impact: A deliberately invulnerable entity (another plugin, a scripted NPC) stays vulnerable after being shot once

title: setNoDamageTicks(0) removes i-frames (intentional)
fix: Make it configurable per weapon.
observation: `setNoDamageTicks(0)` before every hit removes i-frames.
impact: 8 shotgun pellets each deal full damage in one tick; intentional but easy to mis-tune

title: UUID.fromString on raw NBT can throw out of the interact handler
fix: try/catch and treat as an unknown weapon.
observation: `UUID.fromString(value)` on raw NBT with no try/catch.
impact: A corrupt or hand-crafted `uuid` tag throws out of `PlayerInteractEvent`

title: Async watchdog timers call Timer.stop/cancel
fix: Verify Keystone Timer thread-safety; otherwise use start(false).
observation: Several watchdogs use `RepeatingTimer.start(true)` (async). They only flip flags, mutate `ConcurrentHashMap`s, and call `Timer.stop()`/`cancel()` — but `FullAutoTask.cancel()` runs `onCancel` and `handleIncendiaryAuto`'s watchdog calls `running.stop()` on a Bukkit-scheduled task from an async thread.
impact: Borderline against `feedback_repeating_timer_async`; verify Keystone's `Timer.stop` is thread-safe

title: The hitscan origin is the eye while the tracer starts at the muzzle
fix: Use one origin for both.
observation: Hitscan uses `shooter.getEyeLocation()` as the ray origin, not `WeaponMuzzle.compute`, while `WeaponMuzzle`'s javadoc claims every action uses it and `drawTracerLine` renders the first leg from the muzzle.
impact: Tracer visual does not match the actual ray; melee/incendiary/biological also use the eye

title: Hardcoded English strings and a literal section sign in BiologicalAction
fix: Route through Messages and ChatUtil.color.
observation: Hardcoded English user-facing strings bypass `Messages`; `BiologicalAction.java:74` emits a literal `§`.
impact: Violates `feedback_settings_contract` and `feedback_chat_color_codes`; unlocalizable

title: Raw Sound.ENTITY_GENERIC_EXPLODE
fix: Use SoundEffect.
observation: Raw `Sound.ENTITY_GENERIC_EXPLODE` via `world.playSound`.
impact: Violates `feedback_sound_via_configuration` / `feedback_xseries_required`

title: shootInterval schedules a new timer per shot (dormant)
fix: Reuse one timer and fix the magazine-vs-consume comparison.
observation: `shootInterval` schedules a **new** `CountdownTimer` per shot whenever `consumeOnTime > -1`, each of which clears the held slot when it fires. Also `weaponConsumedOnShot > 0 && currentMagCapacity == weaponConsumedOnShot` compares a magazine count against a consume count.
impact: Timer pile-up and a semantically odd condition; both branches are dormant because every shipped YAML sets `Time: -1` and `Consume_On_Shot: 0`

title: An unknown Category becomes OTHER; bad materials become FEATHER or IRON_PICKAXE
fix: Reject unknown categories and materials with a WARN and skip the file.
observation: An unrecognised `Category` silently becomes `OTHER`, which is parsed by `GunWeaponParser` — a typo produces a gun that then fails on the missing `Projectile` section. Likewise an unresolvable `Material` silently becomes `FEATHER` and an unresolvable ammo material becomes `IRON_PICKAXE`.
impact: Confusing failure modes for admins; only an `info`-level log line

title: Parse failures are logged at info and tab-completion still offers the weapon
fix: Log at WARN and complete from the loaded registry.
observation: Parse failures are logged at `info` and the weapon is simply missing from the registry; `/glw weapon give` still tab-completes it from the file list.
impact: Silent partial config loss

title: Throwables share one UUID per type, so press, scope and spread state is shared between players
fix: Key throwable state per player (UUID + player).
observation: Every gate is keyed by **weapon UUID**, and throwables deliberately share one UUID per type. `ScopeData`, `SpreadManager` and `RecoilManager` are likewise per-`Weapon`-instance.
impact: Two players holding the same throwable type share the press gate, scope state, spread and recoil index

title: Durability.Base 0 divides by zero and silently yields 0
fix: Validate > 0.
observation: `scale = itemMax / weaponMax` with no guard for `weaponMax == 0` (`Durability.Base: 0` is accepted by the parser via `min(0)`).
impact: Division by zero → `Infinity` → undefined `(short)` cast

title: RecoilManager.clone without Cloneable
fix: Implement Cloneable or delete it.
observation: `clone()` calls `super.clone()` but the class does not implement `Cloneable`.
impact: Dead code that would throw `PluginException` if ever called

title: Per_Shot affects the SINGLE press-lock window
fix: Use 1 for the SINGLE lock.
observation: `Per_Shot` is only consulted for BURST (`WeaponInteract.shoot:666`), but it *is* used to compute the SINGLE press-lock window (`:593`).
impact: Confusing semantics; the shotgun's press lock is 6 ticks rather than 3

title: A fractional Cooldown is truncated to 0
fix: Parse as ticks with rounding (or document integer ticks) and log.
observation: `Cooldown` is read as a double and cast to `int`, so sub-1 values become 0. `FullAutoTask` then clamps to 1 tick internally, but `shootOtherModes` computes `lockTicks = max(perShot*0, 4) = 4`.
impact: Fractional cooldowns are silently meaningless; the intent behind `0.3` is lost

title: The cosmetic id is unregistered before the task ends
fix: Unregister when the task finishes.
observation: `onProjectileHit` unregisters the cosmetic id, but `SteppedProjectileTask` may still be running for a few more ticks.
impact: Post-hit vanilla damage events for that entity are no longer suppressed

title: Plugin fire is not reverted on shutdown
fix: Revert placed FIRE blocks in onShutdown.
observation: Clears the tracking map without reverting the placed FIRE blocks; scheduled removal tasks die with the plugin.
impact: Plugin fire left in the world becomes normal spreading fire after a restart

title: A Config_Version key skips the file silently
fix: Log at WARN.
observation: `Config_Version` presence silently skips the whole file with no log line.
impact: An admin adding a version stamp to a weapon file loses that weapon with no diagnostic

title: Carried-ammo count uses full ItemStack equality
fix: Match by the ammo NBT tag.
observation: Carried-ammo counting uses `item.equals(ammo.buildItem(item.getAmount()))` — a full `ItemStack` equality including display name and lore. `buildItem` here resolves placeholders with `player = null` while the ammo the player holds may have been built with a player.
impact: Placeholder-bearing ammo names would make the count come out as 0 and block shell-by-shell reloads

title: Dead flare ammunition entry
fix: Remove it or reference it.
observation: The `flare` entry is registered but no shipped weapon references it (`FLARE` projectile weapons use other ammo).
impact: Dead config entry

title: The five action types diverge on ammo, durability, events and damage
fix: Extract one shared shot pipeline used by all five actions.
observation: Only `GunAction` consumes magazine ammo correctly, writes NBT back, honours `Durability.Change.On_Shot` on every shot, fires `WeaponShootEvent`, and gets the default damage pipeline (crit, headshot, wearable reduction, fire ticks, impact sound). `MeleeAction` skips ammo and `WeaponShootEvent`; `ThrowableAction` skips ammo, durability, `WeaponShootEvent` and the raytracer; `IncendiaryAction` writes NBT and honours `Consume_Rate` (via `IncendiaryWeapon.consumeShot`) but deals no real damage; `BiologicalAction` skips NBT writes and deals no damage (corrected during verification).
impact: Any refactor of `GunAction` alone leaves four divergent code paths (per `feedback_unify_across_weapon_types`)

title: destroyAll pass 1 ejects are cancelled by the dismount listener
fix: Unregister the sessions (or set a bypass flag) before ejecting so the listener lets the eject through.
observation: Pass 1 calls `live.eject()` while the sessions are still in `VehicleRegistry`, so the dismount listener sees a non-sneaking, non-dead player and cancels every one of those ejects. The stated purpose of the two-pass design (unmount everyone before persisting, to avoid `RootVehicle` NBT) is therefore not achieved by pass 1; the passenger is only really removed later by `MinecartVehicle.despawn()` after `vehicleRegistry.clear()`.
impact: Fragile ordering: any future change that persists or returns before the despawn loop reintroduces the rogue-duplicate-minecart bug the code was written to fix.

title: The CarQuitListener eject is dead code
fix: Same fix as GD-01; remove the dead eject.
observation: Same cause — the first `live.eject()` is cancelled by the dismount listener; only `parkCar`'s trailing eject (after `unregister`) works. The listener's own eject is dead code.
impact: Misleading; masks issue #1.

title: The car item is destroyed when the inventory is full on pickup or destroy
fix: Drop leftovers like CarGiveCommand.giveCarItem does.
observation: `player.getInventory().addItem(...)` return value (the leftover map) is discarded — with a full inventory the car item is destroyed. `CarGiveCommand.giveCarItem:122-126` does handle leftovers by dropping them, showing the intended pattern.
impact: Item loss.

title: An empty jetpack grants permanent fall immunity
fix: Cancel fall damage only while hasFuel (and recently flying).
tests: STILL OPEN 0.9.2 WS8 (2026-09-20): unrelated to this row's jetpack code, but noted because the new grappling hook (gate G2-G3, commit 122bf53d) was deliberately designed to avoid the same failure shape - its landing grace is one-shot and bounded by Fall_Damage_Grace_Ticks rather than an unconditional/permanent immunity. The jetpack's own fall-immunity bug is untouched by WS8.
observation: A jetpack session exists for as long as the chestplate is worn, regardless of fuel. All FALL damage is cancelled, so simply wearing an empty jetpack grants permanent fall immunity.
impact: Gameplay exploit.

title: A zero-fuel jetpack still glides and steers
fix: Gate the descent cap and air control on hasFuel.
tests: STILL OPEN 0.9.2 WS8 (2026-09-20): unrelated to this row's jetpack code, but noted because the new grappling hook (gate G2-G3, commit 122bf53d) was deliberately designed to avoid the same failure shape - GrappleService.isActive is bounded by Max_Duration_Ticks with no glide/steer mechanic at all. The jetpack's own zero-fuel glide/steer bug is untouched by WS8.
observation: With zero fuel the player still gets a capped slow descent (`maxDescentSpeed`, default −0.5 vs vanilla terminal ≈ −3.9) and full WASD air control, because those branches never check `hasFuel`.
impact: Fuel becomes almost irrelevant; free glider.

title: Any player can mount, pick up or refuel any placed car
fix: Check car_owner/placer_uuid (and gangland.cars.<id>) on mount, pickup and refuel; allow gang members and an admin bypass.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 wave 3, commit 8a731fd5; CarAccessPolicy + CarGangContract on mount/refuel/pickup; CarAccessPolicyTest
observation: No ownership/permission check on mount, pickup or refuel. `car_owner` NBT and `placer_uuid` are stored but never read. `gangland.cars.<id>` is only checked at placement.
impact: Any player can steal/drive/pick up any placed car.

title: The wearable permission is only checked on inventory clicks
fix: Validate on right-click equip, InventoryDrag and dispenser paths, and strip unpermitted armour periodically.
observation: The permission gate only covers `InventoryClickEvent` (cursor→armour slot and shift-click). Right-click-to-equip, drag-equip, dispensers and command/shop grants bypass `gangland.wearables.<key>` entirely.
impact: Permission bypass.

title: The input packet class is missing on 1.16 and jetpack input is inert below 1.21.2
fix: Fall back to PlayerToggleSneakEvent/PlayerMoveEvent for jetpack input and log when the interceptor is unavailable.
observation: On 1.16 (the declared support floor) that class does not exist under Mojang mappings, so `packetClass` is null and **no** car steering or jetpack input is ever parsed. On 1.17–1.21.1 the packet exists but vanilla clients only send it while riding a vehicle — so cars work, jetpack jump/sneak/WASD do not. `activate`/`mountCar` fail silently when `getChannel` returns null too.
impact: Cars unsteerable and jetpacks inert on a large part of the declared supported range; no diagnostic is emitted.

title: Refuelling a stack of cans fuels all N (duplication)
fix: Split one can off the stack before writing the fuel NBT.
observation: `ItemBuilder` mutates the underlying `ItemStack` and NBT is per-stack, so refuelling a stack of N fuel cans consumes one coal and grants `fuelPerItem` to all N cans. `CarEntityInteractListener:87` has the mirror problem (a stack of cans loses fuel as if it were one).
impact: Fuel duplication (and, in the transfer direction, loss).

title: Car items carry FUEL_ID and pass as fuel cans
fix: Use a distinct tag or check for the car tag in Fuel.isFuelItem.
location: `Car.buildItem:103-107` stamps `FuelKey.FUEL_ID`, and `Fuel.isFuelItem` only checks that tag
observation: A fuel-enabled car *item* is indistinguishable from a fuel can: `CarEntityInteractListener:57` will happily pump fuel from a spare car item into a parked car of the same type, `FuelRefuelListener` will refuel car items with coal, and `FuelHoldDisplayListener` shows a gauge for them.
impact: Unintended fuel-economy paths; possible exploit combined with #9.

title: ParkedCar yaw Float/double mismatch on MySQL
fix: Use Number casts.
location: `ParkedCarTable:21` declares `yaw` as `Attribute<Float>` but `getData:55` writes `(double) data.getYaw()` and `ParkedCarRepository.doLoadAll:43` reads `(float)(double) result[6]`
observation: The column type and the value type disagree. On SQLite everything is REAL so it works; on a MySQL backend where the driver returns a `Float`, the `(double)` cast throws `ClassCastException` and **all** parked cars fail to load.
impact: Backend-specific startup failure.

title: A jetpack without Fuel_Key starts a session that never flies
fix: Treat an empty Fuel_Key as "not a jetpack" or fail the load.
tests: FIXED 0.9.2 gate G2 (jetpack rehomed from Bartizan's WearableAddon into gadget's own JetpackAddon), commit 4d4ffa28: JetpackAddon.loadJetpacks now treats a missing/blank Fuel_Key as a load error (warn + skip the entry) instead of silently starting a dead fuel session. JetpackAddonLoadTest ("Fuel_Key" mandatory, field round-trip).
observation: A `Jetpack:` section without `Fuel_Key` yields an empty-string key, so `isJetpack()` is true, a session starts and `setAllowFlight(true)` is granted, but `buildItem` skips the fuel tags (it requires a non-empty key), so the wearable can never hold fuel.
impact: Config foot-gun: a jetpack that grants flight state and fall immunity but never flies.

title: Orphan minecarts across chunk boundaries produce duplicates
fix: Search neighbouring chunks (or by entity UUID) and remove orphans with no record.
observation: A minecart that drifted into a neighbouring chunk before the last save is not reclaimed, so a second car is spawned at the DB location. The javadoc also promises removal of orphans without a matching record; no such code exists.
impact: Duplicate cars after a crash.

title: destroyCar's early return leaks the registry entry
fix: Unregister before the task null check.
observation: `if (task == null) return;` happens *before* `vehicleRegistry.unregister` and `despawn`, so a session with a null task leaks both the registry entry and the world entity.
impact: Entity/registry leak (only reachable via an unusual construction path).

title: setAllowFlight(false) is unconditional (creative, downed)
fix: Restore the previous allowFlight state.
observation: `setAllowFlight(false)` is unconditional. A creative-mode player (who can reach `activate` through `JetpackActivateListener.onJoin`, which has no gamemode filter) or a downed player whose respawn config sets `allowFlight(true)` loses flight when the jetpack ends.
impact: Breaks other systems' flight state.

title: Raw Sound constants
fix: Use SoundEffect.
observation: Raw Bukkit `Sound` enum constants are used instead of Keystone `SoundEffect`/XSeries, contrary to the project's stated convention, and are not configurable.
impact: Version-drift risk on enum renames; no config surface.

title: Hardcoded English strings
fix: Route through Messages / CarMessageContract.
observation: Hardcoded English user-facing strings that bypass the `Messages` enum, unlike the car listeners which route through `CarMessageContract`.
impact: Untranslatable UI.

title: No car placement limit, validity check or cooldown
fix: Add Max_Cars per player and a spawn validity check.
observation: No limit on how many cars a player may place, no spawn-location validity check (block occupancy, world guard, distance), and no cooldown.
impact: Entity spam / grief vector.

title: A null UUID could NPE in the tick task (theoretical)
fix: Guard it.
observation: `entity.getEntityUUID()` is passed to `forcePark`/`parkCar`, which do `ConcurrentHashMap.get(uuid)` — a null UUID (possible only if the wrapped minecart reference were null) would throw NPE inside the tick task.
impact: Tick-task exception storm.

title: Car.maxHealth and glideDescentRate are dead config
fix: Implement or remove them.
tests: PARTIALLY MOOT 0.9.2 (WS7 G6 docket review): the glideDescentRate/jetpack half is MOOT, not fixed - WearableAddon.glideDescentRate no longer exists in that form since the jetpack moved to gadget's own JetpackAddon/Jetpack domain type (gate G2, commit 4d4ffa28); whether JetpackAddon carries its own live-or-dead glide field was not audited and should not be assumed fixed. UPDATE 2026-09-20 (WS8 G1 side check): now verified directly - Jetpack.java and JetpackAddon.java carry no glide-descent-rate field at all (only a Sounds.Glide sound block, unrelated to descent, and a runtime-only glideModeActive toggle in JetpackSession/JetpackTask with no config-driven rate); the specific dead-config instance this row named is confirmed gone, not merely unaudited. The Car.maxHealth/CarAddon half is UNCHANGED by this wave and remains open.
observation: Both are read from YAML, documented in the file headers, stored on the model, and never consumed by any code path.
impact: Dead config keys that mislead server owners.

title: The fuel_refuel_amount help entry is missing
fix: Add it to commands.json.
observation: No `fuel_refuel_amount` entry although `FuelRefuelCommand.refuelAmount()` registers the positional argument; the help layer therefore omits it.
impact: Missing help entry (violates the project's commands.json rule).

title: setChestplate on every fuel tick
fix: Batch the NBT writes (every N ticks).
observation: `player.getInventory().setChestplate(updated)` runs on every fuel-burning tick, forcing a full armour-slot resync packet per player per tick.
impact: Performance / packet churn with many jetpack users.

title: A chunk is force-loaded per parked car at startup
fix: Load lazily on ChunkLoadEvent.
observation: `spawnLoc.getChunk().load()` force-loads one chunk per persisted car synchronously during bean construction.
impact: Startup stall proportional to the number of parked cars.

title: Non-sneak dismounts are cancelled for every cause
fix: Cancel only player-initiated dismounts (plugin-eject flag / not dead).
observation: Non-sneak dismounts are cancelled for *any* cause — including plugin-initiated ejects, teleports and vehicle transfers. Combined with #1/#2 this makes "get the player out of the car" require unregistering the session first, which is an undocumented precondition.
impact: Interoperability with other plugins; hard-to-diagnose stuck players.

title: Fuel and durability are not persisted while driving; per-hit writes when parked
fix: Periodic session save; debounce parked writes.
observation: Nothing is persisted while driving; a crash restores the values from the last park/place. Conversely `refuelParkedCar` and `damageParkedCar` save on every single event (per-hit DB write).
impact: Data loss on crash; write amplification on damage.

title: MinecartVehicle.getLocation may return null
fix: Guard the callers.
location: `MinecartVehicle.getLocation():102` returns `null` when the minecart is null
observation: Callers such as `VehicleMovementTask.tickBurnout:106/108` dereference it (`entity.getLocation().getWorld()`), relying entirely on the `isAlive()` guard earlier in the tick.
impact: Latent NPE if the guard order ever changes.

title: pendingRightClickInteract token race
fix: Consume the token in one place.
tests: STILL OPEN 0.9.2 (WS7 G6 docket review): the field moved from CarDamageListener to the new shared CarDamageState (gate G5, commit d136fc8d), centralizing read/consume across both CarDamageListener and the new CarWeaponDamageListener - this prevents the G5 listener split from making the race structurally worse but does NOT fix the underlying race (two events still race on the same game tick). Fix direction unchanged.
observation: Entries are added on every right-click of a car and removed by a 1-tick scheduled task; `onWeaponRaytraceImpact` only *reads* the flag while `onVehicleDamage` *removes* it, so the two consumers race for the same one-tick token.
impact: Occasional missed suppression (a shot damaging the car the player is entering).

title: slotCache is cleared only on quit
fix: Add an expiry.
observation: Cleared only by `FuelHoldDisplayListener.onQuit`. If that listener is ever removed or fails to fire, per-player entries accumulate. Stale slot hints are validated on read, so correctness is fine.
impact: Minor memory growth.

title: Waypoint teleport, select and list ignore the permission and gang checks
fix: Apply waypoint.getPermission() and the gang check in the action bodies, not only in the completers.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 wave 3, commit 8a731fd5; new WaypointAccess applied in teleport/select/list; WaypointAccessTest
observation: The teleport, select and list paths perform **no** `waypoint.getPermission()` or gang check. Permission/gang filtering exists only in the tab-completers. `/glw waypoint list` prints every waypoint with a click-to-run teleport component
impact: Any player with the command node can teleport into another gang's base or a permission-gated area, and can enumerate all of them

title: The cracking mini-game is unreachable (dead feature)
fix: Wire crackingEnabled from LootChestSettings and feed addProgress from a listener, or remove the feature.
observation: The cracking mini-game is unreachable: `setCrackingEnabled`/`setCrackingTimeSeconds` have no callers, `LootChestSettings` does not override `isCrackingEnabled()`, and `completeCracking`/`addProgress` are never invoked. Five events, four handler chains and a full session class are dead code
impact: Whole advertised feature is inert; if enabled it would always time out because no listener feeds progress

title: Buying more than fits voids items after payment
fix: Check space for the full amount in canExecute; drop leftovers or refund.
observation: `canExecute` for GIVE only requires one free slot (`firstEmpty() != -1`), while `execute` does `item.setAmount(sign.getAmount())` and discards the leftover map returned by `addItem`
impact: Buying more than fits silently voids items **after** the money has been withdrawn

title: Sell signs pay before taking the item; aspect priorities are never applied
fix: Use getSortedAspects() in AspectBasedSignHandler.
observation: `SellSign` lists DEPOSIT before TAKE and `AspectBasedSignHandler` runs aspects in list order; `SignTypeDefinition.getSortedAspects()` (which would apply the priorities) is never called anywhere
impact: Money is paid before the item is removed; if TAKE fails between `canHandle` and `execute` the player keeps both

title: The respawn time is written as long and read as int, so it is always 300
fix: Read with getLongTagData.
observation: The respawn time is written as a long NBT tag and read as an integer, so the read returns 0 and falls back to the 300 s default
impact: Admin-configured respawn times are silently ignored

title: Static Player-keyed maps in WaypointTeleport (leak, cooldown bypass by relog)
fix: Key by UUID, make them instance fields and clear on quit.
observation: `teleportCooldown`, `countdownTimer` and `totalDistance` are **static** `HashMap<Player, ...>` with no quit cleanup
impact: Memory leak on stale `Player` objects; warm-up timers survive logout; cooldowns are bypassed by relogging (new `Player` identity)

title: refactorIds mutates the waypoint map async and NPEs on a missing twin
fix: Run on the main thread and stop renumbering ids (use stable ids).
observation: `refactorIds()` runs inside `runQueriesAsync` and mutates the `waypoints` `HashMap` (remove/put) plus the static id counter; `waypoints.get(id)` may return null and is dereferenced immediately
impact: Data race with main-thread reads; `NullPointerException` when a DB row has no in-memory twin; all ids shift under external references

title: Three permission node shapes for waypoints
fix: Standardise on gangland.waypoint.<name> everywhere.
observation: Three different permission node shapes for the same concept: `gangland.waypoint.<name>` (created), `gangland.waypoint.<id>` (removed), `waypoint.<id>` (registered at load)
impact: Permissions are never actually cleaned up and never line up with what `Waypoint.getPermission()` returns

title: gang_id -1 violates the FK on MySQL
fix: Write NULL for non-gang waypoints.
observation: `gang_id` has a foreign key to `gang.id` and is nullable, but `getData` always writes the sentinel `-1` for non-gang waypoints instead of `null`
impact: Foreign-key violation on save wherever FKs are enforced (MySQL certainly)

title: yaw/pitch Float vs double casts
fix: Use Number casts.
observation: `yaw`/`pitch` are declared `Attribute<Float>` but written as `(double)` and read back with a `(double)` cast
impact: `ClassCastException` on load if the driver returns `Float` (MySQL `FLOAT` column)

title: Looted chests get no hologram or timer after restart
fix: On load start a cooldown or reset is_looted.
observation: On startup a chest loaded with `is_looted = true` and (necessarily) `cooldownEndTime = 0` gets neither an "available" hologram nor a cooldown timer, yet is fully openable
impact: Silent hologram loss after every restart for previously looted chests

title: A null world NPEs in hologram spawn
fix: Guard getWorld() (skip and log).
observation: `chestData.getLocation().clone().add(...)` is passed to `HologramService` with no `getWorld()` null check, and `LootChestRepository.doLoadAll:58-59` can build a `Location` with a null world
impact: NPE / hologram spawn failure for chests whose world was renamed or removed

title: The first viewer's close starts the cooldown; respawn re-syncs stale viewers
fix: Start the cooldown when the last viewer closes and close remaining viewers before respawn.
observation: `closeSession` starts the chest cooldown on the **first** viewer's close while others are still looting; `completeCooldown` calls `chestData.respawn()` before the callback force-closes the remaining viewers, whose `close()` then re-syncs their items onto the freshly respawned chest
impact: Loot duplication / stale inventory restored onto a respawned chest

title: Removing a chest leaves active sessions
fix: Close sessions and clear the maps in unregisterChest.
observation: `unregisterChest` does not close active sessions or clear `sharedChestInventories`/`activeSessionsByChest` for the removed chest
impact: Players keep looting a deleted chest; on close a cooldown and hologram are recreated at the deleted location

title: Quitting with a chest open never starts the cooldown
fix: Run the completion handler in cancelSession.
observation: `cancelSession` on quit calls `session.close()` (syncing the inventory) but skips `sessionCompleteHandler` and the cooldown start
impact: Quitting with a chest open leaves it permanently un-cooled-down until someone else closes it

title: Allowed_Tiers and tierId are never applied
fix: Filter entries by tier in generateLoot.
observation: `generateLoot(String tierId, ...)` never uses `tierId`; `LootTable.allowedTiers` is loaded from `Allowed_Tiers` and never read
impact: `Allowed_Tiers` in `loot_chests.yml` is a no-op — any tier can roll any table

title: Minimum >= Maximum throws inside the handler
fix: Validate at load and guard nextDouble.
observation: `random.nextDouble(min, max)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` when `Minimum >= Maximum`
impact: A plausible config (`Minimum: 100, Maximum: 100`) makes every chest open throw inside the event handler

title: openedLootChests is keyed by Player and rewards on open without taking
fix: Key by UUID and reward on close/take.
observation: `openedLootChests` is a `Map<Player, Set<UUID>>` pruned only by chest id on cooldown completion
impact: `Player` reference leak; and because the reward fires on `LootChestOpenEvent`, opening-and-closing without taking anything still pays out

title: Any player can create a shop sign and there is no break protection
fix: Check the permission on SignChangeEvent (SIGN_NO_PERM) and add a BlockBreakEvent guard for owner/admin.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 wave 3, commit 8a731fd5; SignPermissions + SignProtection listener; SignCreationTest (red-first) + SignProtectionTest
observation: No permission check on sign creation, and no handler at all for sign breaking. `Messages.SIGN_NO_PERM` ("Errors.Permissions.Sign") is declared but never used
impact: Any player who can place a sign can create a functioning shop; any player who can break blocks can delete one

title: Interaction re-parses but never validates signs (negatives honoured)
fix: Run validateSign in the interact path or validate inside the parser.
observation: The interact path calls `parseSign` only — `validateSign` is never re-run. `AbstractSignParser.parsePrice/parseAmount` accept negatives and zero
impact: A sign created outside `SignChangeEvent` (schematic, WorldEdit, `/setblock`, another plugin) is honoured with arbitrary price/amount

title: Editing a formatted [BUY] sign fails validation
fix: Strip brackets in validateSignType.
observation: `validateSignType` strips colors but not brackets; `normalize` strips brackets. A player editing an already-formatted `[BUY]` sign passes registry lookup and then fails validation
impact: Existing signs cannot be edited in place; the sign is cancelled and reverts

title: Unguarded Enum.valueOf on sign content
fix: Same as WB-21.
observation: `Enum.valueOf(sign.getContent().toUpperCase())` with no try/catch in both `execute` and `canExecute`
impact: `IllegalArgumentException` propagates out of the interact listener for any malformed content line

title: Loot chest events are Cancellable but never checked
fix: Honour isCancelled after callEvent.
observation: Every loot-chest event implements `Cancellable`, but `callEvent` results are never inspected
impact: The cancellation contract is a lie; add-ons cannot veto opens, cooldowns or cracking

title: cooldown_bypass is registered but force_rank is checked
fix: Check the registered node.
observation: The command registers `<node>.cooldown_bypass` but the bypass check reads `gangland.command.teleport.force_rank`
impact: The registered permission does nothing; the effective one is undiscoverable

title: Async CountdownTimer callbacks mutate plain HashMaps
fix: Use start(false).
observation: `CountdownTimer.start(true)` (async) is used for callbacks that mutate plain `HashMap`s (`reconfirm`, `deleteWaypointId`, `deleteWaypointTimer`)
impact: Violates the project's own "async timers are only for flag flips" rule; corrupt map state under concurrency

title: Reconfirm is keyed by player only, skipping the price confirm for another waypoint
fix: Key by (player, waypoint).
observation: The reconfirm gate is keyed by player only, not by (player, waypoint)
impact: Confirming a cheap teleport then naming an expensive one skips its price confirmation

title: createWaypointName.get(player).get() can NPE
fix: Null-guard.
observation: `createWaypointName.get(player).get()` with no null guard
impact: NPE if the confirm branch is reached without a stored name

title: Invulnerability is never cleared on quit or reload
fix: Clear on quit and in onShutdown/onPreClear.
observation: The shield sets `player.setInvulnerable(true)` with a main-thread timer to clear it, but nothing clears it on quit or plugin reload
impact: A player can end up permanently invulnerable across a reload

title: The Countdown_Timer config key is unread
fix: Use it or remove it.
observation: `LootChestConfig.defaultCountdownTime` (from `Loot_Chest.Countdown_Timer`) has no readers anywhere
impact: Dead config key that looks authoritative to server owners

title: The wand writes to the currently held item, not the GUI's item
fix: Capture the ItemStack at GUI open.
tests: FIXED 0.10.0 CUT, commit 5d6cbefc: openConfigInventory captures wandSlot once (getHeldItemSlot()) and threads it through every nested screen instead of re-reading getItemInMainHand()/setItemInMainHand(); pinned on updateWandLore only (LootChestWandTest) - setWandNBT/handleInvSizeChange/openConfigInventory read getItem(wandSlot) but are unpinned, thin pins owed by WS3 G5 (orchestrator ruling W50). Relocated to gangland-features/gangland-lootchest (branch 0.10.0-ws3, commit ab589b4d)
observation: `setWandNBT` re-reads `getItemInMainHand()` rather than operating on the item that opened the GUI; the same is true of `handleInvSizeChange`, `updateWandLore` and the `getRespawnTimeFromWand(heldItem)` captured at GUI-build time
impact: Swapping the held item mid-configuration writes to the wrong item or silently no-ops

title: Allowed-block substring match
fix: Use an exact Material match.
tests: FIXED 0.10.0 CUT, commit 5d6cbefc: LootChestWandListener's allowed-block check changed from .contains(allowed.toUpperCase()) to .equalsIgnoreCase(allowed) - CHEST no longer wrongly matches TRAPPED_CHEST/ENDER_CHEST; LootChestWandListenerTest (red via contains()). Relocated to gangland-features/gangland-lootchest (branch 0.10.0-ws3, commit ab589b4d)
observation: Allowed-block matching is `block.getType().name().contains(allowed)`, a substring test
impact: `CHEST` matches `ENDER_CHEST` and `TRAPPED_CHEST`, and `SHULKER_BOX` matches every coloured shulker; narrowing the list has no effect

title: Zero-weight tables always return the last entry
fix: Fall back to a uniform choice.
observation: `selectWeightedRandom` falls through to the last element when the cumulative weight walk overshoots
impact: A table with all-zero weights always returns the same entry

title: Bulk actions are identical to single clicks
fix: Implement a quantity or drop the feature.
observation: `executeBulkAction` re-runs the identical aspect chain a single click already runs
impact: "Bulk" adds a confirmation prompt but no different quantity or price behaviour

title: One bad sign format aborts all remaining registrations
fix: Catch per format and continue.
observation: `initialize()` swallows `SignValidationException` from `setupSigns()` with a generic warning, aborting all remaining registrations
impact: A single bad format leaves the sign system silently half-registered

title: WaypointTeleport leaks its warm-up state on a cancelled TeleportEvent or a missing world: the next 1.5 blocks of walking prints 'teleport cancelled' for a finished timer and the distance accumulator carries over (LS-06 sibling)
fix: W5-K (api body change, no signature change): clear countdownTimer and totalDistance on the cancelled-event and world-missing paths of teleport(), and clear totalDistance on the success path too; the same fix works before W5's vetoes make cancelled TeleportEvents routine. LS-06's UUID-keying still stands separately. [found by the Gangs+ parity pass 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W5-K of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
tests: WaypointTeleportCancelTest (cancelled and world-missing paths leave no countdownTimer or totalDistance entry)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, Gangs+ parity pass; code-checked against master] teleport() puts the timer into the static countdownTimer map at L72 when the waypoint has a warm-up; the world-missing return (L114-119) and the cancelled-TeleportEvent return (L130-134) leave before the only countdownTimer.remove at L158, and totalDistance is cleared only in onPlayerMove L106, never on a teleport path. The entry survives, so the player's next movement past the 1.5-block threshold cancels a finished timer and prints WAYPOINT_TELEPORT_CANCELLED, and a partial totalDistance carries into the next warm-up. Today only gadget's grapple listens for teleport events, so it is latent; the W5 vetoes make it routine. Read from code; not run.

title: A downed player has no command or waypoint-teleport block and can start and complete a waypoint teleport while downed
fix: W5-K: WaypointTeleport (or the caller) refuses a user in DownedPlayerRegistry before the warm-up starts and cancels a running warm-up on downing; body-only api change plus a Messages line. [found by the Gangs+ parity pass 2026-09-30; fixed in lane W5-K of brainstorming/gang-turf-wave-2026-09-30/PLAN.md]
observation: [found 2026-09-30, Gangs+ parity pass; code-checked against master] CustomPlayerDeathListener puts a player into the downed state (DownedPlayerRegistry.add) but no listener blocks commands for downed players: the only PlayerCommandPreprocessEvent handlers are cops DetainmentListener (restrained players) and InventoryOpenByCommandListener, and no downed check appears in any waypoint or teleport command path (grep). A downed player can run a waypoint command and, since the warm-up only cancels on movement, which a downed player cannot do, the teleport completes. Read from code; not run.

title: Weapon.clone shares the tags map, so cloning a built weapon wipes the source's tags
fix: Copy the map in clone() (reassign tags to a new HashMap) before initClone clears it.
tests: WeaponCloneTest clone_bug_tagsMapIsSharedNotCopied (pins BUG; flip when fixed)
observation: Weapon.tags is a final field, so Object.clone() copies only the reference; initClone's tags.clear() empties the one map both the template and the clone share. Cloning a weapon that already had initializeTags/buildItem called silently wipes the template's tag cache. Found by the test initiative; not listed in weapons.md.

title: MailManager.findPendingByGangAndRecipient has no null guard for the recipient
fix: Null-guard the recipient (return empty).
observation: Passing a null recipient throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty result. Called out in the gangs-ranks-mail.md Test Surface and pinned by the mail tests.

title: ParkedVehicle.addFuel has no upper clamp at maxFuel
fix: Clamp the result to maxFuel.
observation: addFuel clamps at zero for negative amounts but never at maxFuel, so a parked car can be over-fuelled past its tank size through refuelParkedCar. Observation-adjacent finding from the gadget tests.

title: TeleportCommand.teleportCost dereferences a null User
fix: Guard user == null before touching user.getUser(); done as part of the LS-01 fix.
tests: FIXED 0.8.3 wave 3, commit 8a731fd5 (guard only, no dedicated test)
