observation: Both callers pass userManager.getUser(player) straight through without a null check, and the first statement in the invalid-waypoint branch is user.getUser().sendMessage(...), so a player with no cached User NPEs on /glw teleport. Same shape as GR-01. Found while applying the LS-01 waypoint access gate.

title: Gang invite-cancel and ally pending-cancel are still ungated after GR-03
fix: Apply GangPermissions.allows with the INVITE / ALLY node the same way the send paths now do.
observation: The GR-03 wave gated every subcommand that creates or breaks gang state (invite, ally request/accept/reject, abandon) but left the two cancel leaves open, so any member can still cancel their gang outgoing invites and alliance requests. Lower impact than the send paths - the state cancelled belongs to the caller own gang - but it is the same hole.

title: FileConfig.weaponLoader registers only 5 of the 22 shipped weapon YAMLs, so a fresh install never writes out or loads 17 weapons
fix: Add addExpectedFile calls (or loop the module's weapon-YAML resource list) for all 22 weapon YAMLs in the module's WeaponFileConfig.weaponLoader; the weapon module flip (commit 0272008b) copied the 5-name list verbatim to stay behaviour-preserving, so this still needs its own fix.
location: gangland-features/gangland-weapon/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/weapon/WeaponFileConfig.java:89-97 (weaponLoader) - moved here from gangland-impl config/FileConfig.java by the weapon module flip (0272008b)
observation: weaponLoader() registers only rifle, grenade, knife, flamethrower and syringe_gun via addExpectedFile even though gangland-impl/src/main/resources/weapon/ ships 22 weapon YAMLs. FolderLoader.loadData only creates files from expectedFolderFiles when the data folder is missing or empty, so on a fresh install the other 17 (awp, crowbar, flashbang, golden_ak47, machete, minigun, molotov, mp5, pistol, ray_gun, revolver, rocket_launcher, sawn_off, shotgun, smoke_grenade, steyr_aug, tomahawk) are never written out and never loaded. observation: refresh() and decorate() both walk the refreshers list in insertion order and return the result of the first refresher whose canRefresh() matches; register() only appends, with no way to insert ahead of or replace an earlier entry. Latent today because every ItemRefresher registration happens in one core @Bean method in a fixed order, but it goes live the moment a feature that registers its own ItemRefresher (e.g. unique weapons) becomes a runtime module loaded after the core registrations - a later, more specific refresher can never outrank an earlier, more general one, so an item could refresh via the wrong refresher. Found 2026-09-07 during module-split planning (brainstorming/module-split-2026-09-07/weapon.md B-5); fixed by the weapon module flip.

title: GameplayConfig.lootChestLoader resolves loot_chests.yml item strings synchronously inside its CONFIG-phase @Bean body, with no ordering edge to a module's item converter
fix: FIXED 0.9.0 (1340d97c, branch 0.9.0): GameplayConfig.lootChestLoader no longer calls fileManager.initializeAll() eagerly - deferred to a @PostConstruct mirroring initializeInventoryLoader(); the executor also found the eager item-resolution path itself was already lazy pre-stream (SlotItemFactory/InventoryLoader resolve loot-chest item strings at roll time), so the entry's original observation is partly stale
tests: covered by the gangland-impl suite at gate G (194 tests green); no dedicated pin
observation: lootChestLoader() calls fileManager.initializeAll() directly inside its own CONFIG-phase @Bean body (gangland-impl/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/config/GameplayConfig.java:272-278), taking only LootChestManager and FileManager as parameters, so loot_chests.yml item refs are parsed at that instant with no ordering edge to any module's item-converter bean. InventoryLoader already avoids this exact trap by deferring its initialize() to a @PostConstruct (GameplayConfig.java ~L287+) that runs once every CONFIG bean is registered and the ItemConverterRegistry is populated; lootChestLoader was never given the same treatment. Found 2026-09-07 during module-split planning (brainstorming/module-split-2026-09-07/gadget.md OQ-2; same triage class also covers the weapon and turf flips) and originally filed as latent, since no shipped loot_chests.yml used a car: ref. Re-verified 2026-09-08 after the gadget and weapon flips landed (commits 4304172c, 0272008b): `grep -c 'Item: "weapon:' gangland-impl/src/main/resources/lootchests/loot_chests.yml` = 44, `Item: "wearable:` = 12, `Item: "ammo:` = 29, `Item: "car:` = 0. weapon:, wearable: and ammo: refs are exactly the item kinds now registered by WeaponModuleConfig.weaponItemRegistrations (itemConverterRegistry.register(WEAPON/AMMUNITION/"ammo"/WEARABLE, ...)) in the weapon runtime module, a bean with no parameter dependency on GameplayConfig.lootChestLoader or vice versa - so whichever way the CONFIG-phase topological sort happens to order these two beans on a given boot, there is no guarantee weaponItemRegistrations runs before lootChestLoader. This is no longer a latent/future risk gated on a car: ref that doesn't exist yet - it is a live ordering hazard against 56 existing item refs across the majority of the game's ~20 configured loot chests, so it is raised from P2 to P1: if the sort ever lands the wrong way (e.g. after any future bean-graph change touching either side), the affected chests silently lose their weapon/wearable/ammo drops instead of failing loudly. No code change made in this task - still open.

title: Keystone ListenerService.registerGuarded dispatches sibling events sharing a HandlerList into the wrong handler (argument type mismatch on every ArmorStand/creature spawn)
fix: Upstream (Keystone keystone-bean ListenerService.registerGuarded): mirror Bukkit JavaPluginLoader and return early from the guarded executor when !eventType.isAssignableFrom(event.getClass()); red-first unit test registers a handler for a subclass event whose HandlerList is inherited from its parent (two fake events sharing one HandlerList) and asserts the sibling event is ignored instead of throwing. Ship as Keystone 1.8.1 and bump keystone.version in the root pom.
tests: - (Keystone keystone-bean ListenerServiceTest sibling-event case, red first)
location: E:/Programming/java/Keystone keystone-bean/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/keystone/bean/listener/ListenerService.java:86-110 (registerGuarded executor lambda) and :113-119 (invokeHandler); observed through gangland-features/gangland-weapon/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/weapon/listener/reload/WeaponItemSpawnListener.java:35 (onItemSpawn(ItemSpawnEvent))
observation: Observed 2026-09-08 01:24:46-47 and 01:27:09-10 on the test server whenever the weapon module is loaded: "[Keystone Common.LoggingSink] argument type mismatch (listener=WeaponItemSpawnListener event=ItemSpawnEvent) [listener.dispatch] java.lang.IllegalArgumentException ... ListenerService.invokeHandler(ListenerService.java:116)" once per hologram ArmorStand spawn (stack: Hologram.createArmorStand <- ChestCooldownManager.showAvailableHologram <- LootChestManager.registerLootChests), six times in ten seconds. Bukkit ItemSpawnEvent does not declare its own HandlerList - it inherits EntitySpawnEvent.getHandlerList() - so pluginManager.registerEvent(ItemSpawnEvent.class, ...) registers the executor on the shared EntitySpawnEvent list and Bukkit invokes it for CreatureSpawnEvent/SpawnerSpawnEvent/EntitySpawnEvent too. Bukkit's own JavaPluginLoader.createRegisteredListeners guards this with eventClass.isAssignableFrom(event.getClass()); the guarded executor in ListenerService omits that check, so Method.invoke throws IllegalArgumentException, the Guard classifies it as a fault and reports it (fault sink + log) for every non-item entity spawn. Affects every Keystone-dispatched handler for an event that shares a parent HandlerList (EntityDamageByEntityEvent/EntityDamageEvent, PlayerInteractAtEntityEvent/PlayerInteractEntityEvent, BlockMultiPlaceEvent/BlockPlaceEvent, ...) across Gangland, Oriel and every module.

title: BukkitRegistryFixture's defaultValue() proxy fallback boxes every remaining primitive as Integer, which throws ClassCastException for a registry-routed short-returning method
fix: Add explicit byte.class/short.class cases (boxed as (byte) 0 / (short) 0) to defaultValue(Class<?>) alongside the existing boolean/void/char/long/float/double cases, mirroring the fix already applied to bartizan-plugin's own copy of this fixture.
tests: none (latent - no bartizan-api test currently drives a short-returning registry method through this fixture)
observation: Found 2026-09-09 while writing bartizan-plugin's own duplicate of this fixture for WeaponItemApiTest (bartizan.md N-gap): Material.getMaxDurability() (called from Weapon.buildItem() via ItemBuilder.getItemMaxDurability()) routes through the registry proxy and returns `short`; the proxy's default-value fallback returned a boxed Integer 0 for every unmatched primitive type, and the JDK dynamic-proxy invocation contract does not coerce a mismatched boxed numeric type, so the call threw "class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Short" at the call site. Fixed in bartizan-plugin's new copy (bartizan-plugin/src/test/java/org/luckyraven/bartizan/testsupport/BukkitRegistryFixture.java); bartizan-api's original copy still has the gap but nothing there currently exercises a short-returning registry method through it.

title: WeaponManager persistence never ran — nothing called RepositoryRegistry.saveAll/DatabaseManager.closeConnections/BartizanDatabase.disconnectBackend, so every runtime weapon state was lost on restart and the SQLite pool outlived a reload
fix: Add a self-scheduling WeaponAutoSaveTask (Keystone Timer) wired via a CONFIG @Bean in WiringConfig that calls RepositoryRegistry.saveAll() every Auto_Save.Time minutes (guarded so <= 0 disables it), and isolate Bartizan.onDisable() into per-stage try/catch: shutdown.beans -> shutdown.save (saveAll) -> shutdown.connections (DatabaseManager.closeConnections) -> shutdown.backend (BartizanDatabase.disconnectBackend), mirroring Gangland's ShutdownSequence stage-isolation shape.
observation: Found 2026-09-09 during the R-B-FINAL review of the Bartizan split (bartizan.md executor X-B-R, task B1, blocker). WeaponManager.initialize() wired setDataSupplier(...) but nothing in the bean graph or the shutdown path ever called saveAll/closeConnections/disconnectBackend — every persisted weapon uuid (and its NBT ammo/durability state) was lost on every restart, and the HikariCP SQLite pool behind the DatabaseBackend outlived a /reload. Red-first: new WeaponAutoSaveTaskTest failed to compile against pre-fix code (class did not exist, verified by temporarily moving the new production file out and back); green after.

title: WeaponDeathListener could override a death message Gangland's own LOWEST-priority listener deliberately nulled (NPC victim, NPC killer, or a duplicate event)
fix: Add `if (event.getDeathMessage() == null) return;` at the top of WeaponDeathListener.onPlayerDeath, immediately after reading the victim, so a null message from an earlier suppressing listener is never overridden.
observation: Found 2026-09-09 during the R-B-FINAL review (bartizan.md executor X-B-R, task M1). WeaponDeathListener runs at EventPriority.HIGH specifically so it runs after Gangland's own PlayerDeathListener (EventPriority.LOWEST), which nulls the death message for an NPC victim, an NPC killer, or a duplicate event; without the guard this listener could set a weapon-attributed message where Gangland deliberately wanted none. Standalone (no Gangland present) the vanilla message is non-null so the weapon path is unaffected. Red-first test WeaponDeathListenerTest.onPlayerDeath_nullDeathMessage_neverOverridden failed the verify(event, never()).setDeathMessage(any()) assertion against pre-fix code (verified via git stash on the listener file); green after.

title: WeaponTableImportTask wrote the one-shot import marker even after a caught SQLException, permanently skipping the legacy weapon-table import on a transient failure
fix: Only call writeMarker(marker) on the file-absent path and the success path; on a caught SQLException, report through Diagnostics + log.error and return without writing the marker, so the import retries on the next boot.
observation: Found 2026-09-09 during the R-B-FINAL review (bartizan.md executor X-B-R, task M2; the always-write-the-marker behavior was itself a recorded judgment call at B15, since bartizan.md §1.9 did not settle the failure case). A transient error (e.g. SQLITE_BUSY while Gangland's own pool still holds gangland.db on the first boot) previously wrote the marker anyway, permanently skipping the legacy weapon-uuid import. Red-first test WeaponTableImportTaskTest.run_importThrows_doesNotWriteMarker failed (expected false but was true — marker existed) against pre-fix code, verified via git stash on the source file (forced with a garbage-bytes gangland.db so the SQLite JDBC driver genuinely throws); green after.

title: CarAddon.loadCars silently substitutes a default Material for an unrecognised config value instead of rejecting the entry
fix: Mirror JetpackAddon's fix: XMaterial.matchXMaterial(materialString).map(XMaterial::get).orElse(null), then warn-and-skip on null instead of silently defaulting to MINECART.
observation: `Material material = XMaterial.matchXMaterial(materialString).orElse(XMaterial.MINECART).get();` - an unrecognised Material: string in items/cars.yml resolves to XMaterial.MINECART instead of null, which makes the very next line's "invalid Material" rejection branch (CarAddon.java:80-83) permanently dead code: a typo'd material name in config silently produces a Minecart-material car entry instead of a startup warning telling the server owner to fix their config. Same bug pattern JetpackAddon had before WS7 G2-G3 fixed it there (JetpackAddon.java:106-110 now does .orElse(null) plus an explicit null-check that warns and skips); the WS7 G2-G3 review named both instances as one docket candidate and the orchestrator explicitly deferred CarAddon's identical bug to this docket row at G6. Found 2026-09-16 during the WS7 gadget wave (G2-G3 review, Minor 3), filed 2026-09-20 (G6 docket step).

title: CarGiveCommand/JetpackGiveCommand's <amount> argument had no lower/upper bound - a negative amount threw NegativeArraySizeException, a huge one risked an unbounded allocation
fix: FIXED 0.9.2 gate G4 fix round 1, commit 6bc1e2d1: amount <= 0 rejected at the command layer (Messages.MUST_BE_NUMBERS) plus a defensive Math.max(0, Math.min(amount, 36 * maxStackSize)) clamp inside both private give-methods, so the method itself can never crash regardless of caller.
tests: JetpackGiveCommandAmountGuardTest/CarGiveCommandAmountGuardTest (reflection-driven, red-first - both threw NegativeArraySizeException before the fix)
observation: Both are non-stackable armour/vehicle items (maxStackSize == 1), so slots = ceil(amount / maxStackSize) turned any negative amount straight into a negative array size on the very first bad input. Found WS7 G4 review (Important 2), fixed the same gate. Filed here 2026-09-20 (G6 docket step) per house rule - a fix isn't "done" until the docket knows about it.

title: CarGiveCommand.giveCarItem calls player.getWorld().dropItemNaturally(...) with no null-check on getWorld(), unlike JetpackGiveCommand which null-checks first
fix: Null-guard player.getWorld() before calling dropItemNaturally, mirroring JetpackGiveCommand.giveJetpackItem's "World world = player.getWorld(); if (world != null) { world.dropItemNaturally(...); }" pattern (house rule feedback_get_world_null_check).
observation: CarGiveCommand.giveCarItem calls `player.getWorld().dropItemNaturally(player.getLocation(), item);` directly with no local variable or null-check, while the sibling JetpackGiveCommand.giveJetpackItem (:127-130) assigns `World world = player.getWorld();` and null-checks before calling world.dropItemNaturally(...). Bukkit's getWorld() is nullable; an unlucky ordering could NPE the give command instead of silently no-opping the drop. Pre-existing, found by the WS7 G6 docs review on 2026-09-20.

title: InventoryClickHandler cancels MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY/COLLECT_TO_CURSOR only when the click lands on the bottom (vanilla) inventory, not when COLLECT_TO_CURSOR is invoked from within the top (custom) inventory itself on a non-draggable slot

Fix here only if the cutover slips.
tests: FIXED-BY-WS2 0.10.0 CUT, commit 5d6cbefc: InventoryClickHandler.java deleted outright; the MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY/COLLECT_TO_CURSOR guard now lives in Keystone's ChestMenu/MenuListener unconditionally, for every menu
observation: The `if (!clickedInventory.equals(inv.getInventory()))` branch only cancels MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY/COLLECT_TO_CURSOR when the clicked inventory is the player's own (bottom) inventory; a COLLECT_TO_CURSOR click issued while the top (custom) inventory itself is focused falls through to the normal per-slot handling below with no equivalent guard, mirroring the same class of bug Keystone's own keystone-inventory E6.1 review found and fixed (F4) in its ChestMenu/MenuListener pair. Found 2026-09-17 during the Keystone E6.1 review (its Notes section: "also present today in Gangland InventoryClickHandler.java:34-43"), filed here 2026-09-20 (WS7/E6.1 docket step). Open until Gangland's WS2 workstream moves the inventory framework onto keystone-inventory.

title: /glw debug inv-data's console branch sends its messages to the tracked players instead of the command sender

title: npc-shops BarterView/SellView keep a WeakHashMap<Player, State> whose State value holds the Player (and a MenuFlow that holds it too), so the value strongly reaches back to the key and nothing is ever weakly reclaimed
fix: Switch to Map<UUID, State> at the WS2 CUT gate; cleanup already relies entirely on the explicit remove() calls in onFlowEnd/onBack/onConfirm/onShutdown, so this is leak-prevention hardening, not a behaviour change.
location: gangland-features/gangland-npc-shops BarterView.java:84 and its SellView equivalent
observation: A WeakHashMap only reclaims an entry once its key becomes otherwise unreachable, but here the State value stored under each Player key holds a reference back to that same Player (directly, and again through a held MenuFlow), so the key is always reachable via its own value and the map can never weakly collect an entry - cleanup depends entirely on every exit path calling remove() explicitly. Pre-existing: the old BarterState had the same field, not new to the WS2 work. Found in the WS2 G4 review. Filed here 2026-09-21 (WS2 docket step).

title: Loot chests accepted deposits after the inventory-api cut
fix: SharedLootInventory now implements InventoryHolder; LootChestListener.onInventoryClick gates on holder identity and cancels every inbound deposit action (place/swap/hotbar/shift-in/drag-in) into the top inventory; take paths and bottom-only rearranging fall through untouched.
tests: FIXED 0.10.0 CUT fix round 1, commit 5d6cbefc: 9-case LootChestListenerTest (red-first per blocked action); report and documentation/migration-0.10.0.md corrected to state the old rule -> new rule and why (stash prevention; regeneration would void deposits). Note the policy is now stricter than before the cut - no deposit at all, versus the old draggableSlots allowlist.
observation: The WS3 G1/G2 move off the deleted InventoryHandler-based LootChestSession onto a bare SharedLootInventory (plain Bukkit.createInventory wrap, no InventoryHolder identity, no click gate) silently widened loot chests from take-only into free, shared dumping-ground storage: click-place, shift-click and drag deposits all went through, whereas the deleted InventoryClickHandler previously cancelled every deposit outside a draggableSlots allowlist (and the old LootChestSession only ever marked generated-loot slots draggable, so even empty slots were deposit-blocked before this cut). title: PermissionAttachment leaked on reload rebuild
fix: removeAttachment on the prior PermissionAttachment inside User's rebuild path, or inside RankPermissionApplier.initialize before creating a new one.

observation: No removeAttachment() call exists anywhere for the PermissionAttachment that RankPermissionApplier.initialize (module) - or the deleted UserManager.initializeUserPermission before it - creates. A /glw reload that rebuilds a User re-runs RankPermissionApplier.initialize for an already-online player and leaks the prior attachment (Bukkit never garbage-collects an attachment that isn't explicitly removed), leaving stale rank permission nodes granted for the rest of the session. Guarded today only by PlayerBootstrapService's cache short-circuit, which avoids the common case but not every rebuild path. Found during the WS5 G1-G3 fix round 1 review (F5); left open per the orchestrator's ruling - fixing it needs auditing every initialize() call site for an existing double-attachment guard first, out of scope for that gate.

title: GangMembershipInstaller crashes Gangland_Warfare enable whenever the gang module is present
fix: GangMembershipInstaller (gangland-features/gangland-gang) is a bare @Configuration class instantiated directly via its own constructor rather than a @Bean factory method, so BeanGraph topological sort -- which derives ordering edges only from @Bean method parameters (house convention) -- has no edge forcing it after IdentityContractConfig.gangMembership() (gangland-impl, zero-arg @Bean). DependencyContainer.createInstance can run GangMembershipInstaller before that bean exists, throwing IllegalStateException and failing Gangland.onEnable outright. Fix: give the installer a @Bean factory method (e.g. a GangConfig bean taking GangMembership/MemberManager/GangManager as parameters, calling install() inside the factory and returning a marker/installer bean) so GangMembership becomes a real graph edge; or fix Keystone bean scanning to also read a bare @Configuration class constructor as ordering edges. Add a red-first boot-phase test asserting a module @Configuration class depending on a core zero-arg @Bean does not throw during BeanFactory.instantiate().
observation: Observed 2026-09-23 08:17 on the test server smoke run (0.10.0 @ 89746105, Keystone 1.11.1, 8 runtime modules incl. gang): Gangland_Warfare v0.10.0 fails Server-thread ERROR "Error occurred while enabling Gangland_Warfare v0.10.0 (Is it up to date?)" -> java.lang.IllegalStateException: Failed to instantiate @Configuration class org.luckyraven.gangland.gang.GangMembershipInstaller -- check that every constructor parameter is already registered in the container, caused by IllegalStateException: Cannot resolve required parameter of type org.luckyraven.gangland.data.gang.GangMembership for constructor in org.luckyraven.gangland.gang.GangMembershipInstaller (DependencyContainer.resolveConstructorParameters). Plugin disables immediately after enable failure; every /glw subcommand then throws "unexpected error" since the command tree never registered. 100% reproducible on this build; blocks every WS5/WS6-merge smoke row that needs a booted plugin.

title: Core PermissionRepository has no data supplier and spams ERROR on every reload/autosave when the gang module is absent
fix: Give core PermissionRepository a fallback zero-arg data supplier (e.g. an empty-list default set alongside its RepositoryRegistry registration in gangland-impl, mirroring the GangMembership inert-until-installed pattern) so RepositoryRegistry.saveAll never throws when the gang module -- the only caller of Permission.setDataSupplier via RankManager.initialize() -- is not installed; RankManager keeps overwriting it with the live supplier once the module loads. Add a red-first test booting BeanFactory/RepositoryRegistry without the gang module present and asserting saveAll() does not log a Permission failure.
location: gangland-impl/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/database/repositories/plugin/PermissionRepository.java (never wired outside the gang module) and gangland-features/gangland-gang/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/gang/rank/RankManager.java:124 (permissionRepo.setDataSupplier(permissions::values), the sole caller)
observation: Observed 2026-09-23 08:22 on the test server (0.10.0 @ 89746105) while isolating the WS6 civilians check around the T-53 boot crash: with the gang module NOT deployed (civilians/cops/gadget/npcshops/lootchest only, boot succeeds), every /glw reload and scheduled autosave logs [Keystone Persistence.RepositoryRegistry] Failed to save data for repository: Permission -> java.lang.IllegalStateException: No data supplier set for repository: PermissionRepository, at AbstractRepository.saveAllFromMemory <- RepositoryRegistry.saveAll <- PeriodicalUpdates.updatingDatabase. Before WS5 G0/G1-G3, Permission and its one caller RankManager were both core-resident and always wired; the split left the repository core-hosted (always registered) but its only supplier-setter module-hosted (conditionally loaded), so any server that genuinely omits the gang module -- which WS5 G1 explicitly designed gadget/civilians/cops-n-crooks to support via the GangMembership holder -- gets this ERROR every reload/autosave cycle forever, not just once.

title: GangConfig.gangItemSourceContribution crashes Gangland_Warfare enable: unqualified UserManager is ambiguous (2 candidates)
fix: GangConfig has 4 @Bean methods taking a raw, unqualified UserManager<Player> parameter -- gangPlaceholderContribution, gangOptionContribution, gangDebugContribution, gangItemSourceContribution (only the last currently crashes; the other 3 are equally vulnerable, they just happen to resolve while only one candidate is registered so far -- a concrete instance of the already-docketed CL-24 JVM-dependent bean order risk). DataConfig.java registers exactly two UserManager beans by design, @Bean(name = "online", isGeneric = true) and @Bean(name = "offline", isGeneric = true), and every other consumer in the codebase (e.g. IdentityContractConfig.userLookupContract) correctly takes @Qualifier("online") UserManager<Player>. Add @Qualifier("online") to the parameter on all 4 GangConfig methods (online is clearly correct for all four -- placeholders/options/debug/menus all concern currently-online players/targets, matching the existing pattern everywhere else). Add a red-first GangConfigBeanGraphTest case (the class already exists per fcc41a32) driving the real BeanFactory against GangConfig with both online/offline UserManager beans registered and asserting it does not throw.
location: gangland-features/gangland-gang/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/gang/GangConfig.java:125 (gangPlaceholderContribution), :135 (gangOptionContribution), :146 (gangDebugContribution), :174 (gangItemSourceContribution) -- all missing @Qualifier; gangland-impl/src/main/java/org/luckyraven/gangland/config/DataConfig.java:65-84 (the two isGeneric=true UserManager beans, "online"/"offline")
observation: Observed 2026-09-23 09:01 on the test server (0.10.0 @ fcc41a32, the T-53/T-54 fix commit) while re-running the 8-module smoke that T-53 previously blocked entirely: with T-53 fixed, boot now proceeds further and hits a NEW crash -- Gangland.onEnable throws java.lang.IllegalStateException: Ambiguous bean for parameter 'arg0' of type UserManager for bean GangConfig.gangItemSourceContribution(): 2 candidates registered. Add @Qualifier to disambiguate, at BeanFactory.resolveParameter <- invokeBean <- instantiate <- GanglandContext.bootstrap <- Gangland.onEnable. Plugin disables immediately, same downstream symptom as T-53 (every /glw subcommand throws unexpected error, command tree never registered). 100% reproducible across 2 separate boots this session (identical stack trace both times). A parallel 7-module run with the gang module entirely absent (so GangConfig never loads at all) had zero errors, confirming this is specific to GangConfig's own beans, not a wider regression. This was masked by T-53 in the previous merge round -- the plugin never reached CONFIG-phase bean instantiation far enough to hit it before this fix.

title: Cops share nothing but 'a cop was hit'; Alert_Range only gates IDLE
fix: Each CopGroup owns a Keystone NpcSquad: sightings (own line of sight within Alert_Range, the crime scene, an attacker) are shared; chase with slots and flank points, search from the last-known spot in widening circles; a cop handed another target (an attacker, a retarget) hunts in a squad of its own seeded where it was handed the target

title: Hostile civilians react only when hit themselves and never alert neighbours
fix: Faction key per civilian type; a hit squads the victim and alerts same-faction allies within their own AI.Combat.Alert_Range (one hop; a same-faction attacker alerts nobody); the squad gives up after AI.Combat.Search_Seconds unseen

title: CopListener.onCopDeath never runs for a cop

The AI sweep releases the dead cop within one AI tick, which is why nothing visibly breaks; Citizens may also suppress the drops.

title: One cancelled wanted-decay tick freezes decay for the rest of the episode
fix: WantedExecutor resets the reused WantedEvent's cancelled flag before each callEvent, so a listener's cancel applies to that tick only (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, commit 354784b7; owner decision 9)
observation: [found 2026-09-27, programme diagnosis] The executor reuses one WantedEvent per timer and never reset its cancelled flag, so once any listener cancelled one decay tick every later tick read as cancelled and the wanted level stopped decaying until the episode ended.

title: Cops freeze shoulder to shoulder in a line on one side of the player
fix: Keystone 1.13.0 formation and engagement (KS-NP-23, KS-NP-25); Gangland 0.12.0 (branch npc-squad-tactics) gives each tier a Tactics block over Cops.Tactics - shipped arcs Lieutenant 200, SWAT 270, Military 330, melee tiers always surround - wired by CopNpcFactory.applyTuning and CopManager's squad formation arc; Tactics.Enabled: false restores 0.11 positioning only
tests: TacticsConfigTest, YamlCopConfigProviderTest, CopNpcFactoryMeleeTest, CopGroupSquadTest; Sandbox record: Keystone docs/phase-h12-npc-tactics.md and Gangland documentation/migration-0.12.0.md section 9
observation: [owner report 2026-09-27, programme issue 4, screenshot cops-clustering.png] Five SWAT frozen shoulder to shoulder in a static line on one side of the player, all at the same range, facing the player, not moving. Root causes in Keystone: KS-NP-23 (slot choice) and KS-NP-25 (hold-band freeze).

title: Cops never talk: no squad commands, no radio for nearby players
fix: SquadRadio (gangland-api, shared with gang shouts) turns Keystone's NpcSquadSignal SPI (KS-NP-24) into chat: CopRadio speaks contact, orders with a delayed ack from the ordered cop, reload, check-fire, casualties, backup, dispatch, escalate, resisting and stand-down lines to every player within Radio.Range (32, bystanders included, owner decision 5), throttled per squad and per player; lines in npc/cop_radio_messages.yml (+ _es); civilians shout through civilian_messages.yml Shouts (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics)
tests: SquadRadioTest, RadioSettingsReadTest, RadioSidesTest, CopRadioTest, CopRadioMessagesTest, CivilianMessagesShoutsTest
observation: [owner report 2026-09-27, programme issue 5] Cops should form a squad and send commands to each other, with a text radio heard by players and cops within a range; nothing of the kind existed.

title: Ranged cops stop to shoot, then fire far slower than their guns
fix: Keystone 1.13.0 moves shooters while they fire (KS-NP-25); Bartizan 0.6.0 drains NPC gun cooldowns in server ticks and re-aims bursts (BZ-NU-05); Gangland 0.12.0 (branch npc-squad-tactics) adds per-tier Fire_Rate_Multiplier (cops 0.1, civilians 0.05 = 1 / AI_Tick_Rate, the 0.11 gun cadence on Bartizan and vanilla bows, via the new gangland-api NpcFireRate helper which halves the scale for the vanilla bow/crossbow fallback so it also keeps 0.11's cadence) and gates ranged fire on Alert_Range instead of Combat_Range
tests: NpcFireRateTest, CombatBehaviorTest, PursuingBehaviorTest, CivilianCombatBehaviorTest; Sandbox record: Keystone docs/phase-h12-npc-tactics.md and Gangland documentation/migration-0.12.0.md section 9 (time-to-kill against 0.11 per tier)
observation: [owner report 2026-09-27, programme issue 6] Ranged cops froze in their band to shoot, and a 6-14 block gap between the firing band and Combat_Range left them standing without firing. Gun cadence is restored exactly (including the vanilla bow/crossbow path, closing the gap the fire-rate scale left open on its own - see the newBug fixed by commit 0a9a62ac); time-to-kill still moves with Keystone's server-tick reaction times and the 20-tick melee cooldown (KS-NP-22, CJ-08).

title: Cops, gangs and factions fight as individuals: no escalation, reinforcement or retreat
fix: Gangland 0.12.0 (branch npc-squad-tactics): cuff first, then the whole group fights after Max_Cuff_Attempts escapes or any hit on a cop, radioing Resisting (CJ-23, owner decision 2); up to Radio.Responder_Max (2) idle, returning or civilian-chasing cops from OTHER groups within 32 blocks join on contact, man down or backup (decision 6, and see T-120: a cop released or rotated out of its own group is never pulled back into it); backup on a cop down, with expiry sending the surplus home; retreat to cover at Retreat.Health_Fraction (0.3) for at most 10 s (decision 7); the cop death hook (T-111). Civilians: FactionSquads shared per faction, Contact-shout recruitment within Shouts.Range (24), retreat
tests: CuffingBehaviorTest, CopRadioRespondersTest, CopManagerSquadTest, CopListenerDeathTest, RetreatSettingsTest, CivilianServiceSquadTest, CivilianDeathListenerTest, CivilianNpcFactoryTuningTest
location: gangland-features/cops-n-crooks (CuffingBehavior, CombatBehavior, CopManager, radio/), gangland-features/gangland-civilians (FactionSquads, CivilianCombatBehavior)
observation: [owner report 2026-09-27, programme issue 7] Smart cops / gangs / factions feedback loop: the AI should coordinate, escalate and reinforce instead of acting cop by cop.

title: Per-tier Cuff_Radius is still ignored by the PURSUING/CUFFING transitions (global Cops.Behaviour.Cuff_Radius always used)
fix: Have PursuingBehavior and CuffingBehavior read the cop's own tierConfig.cuffRadius() instead of the constructor-injected global configProvider.getCuffRadius() (CopBehaviorFactory.java:49-56)
observation: [programme diagnosis 2026-09-27, verified still present on npc-squad-tactics 93fdacbd] Only CopNpc.attemptCuff reads the per-tier value; the PURSUING/CUFFING transition gates still use the single global default. Every shipped tier's Cuff_Radius (3.0-5.0, cops.yml) is >= the global default, so today this silently caps tiers 2-5's larger configured radius to the global one rather than causing a bounce loop; a future tier configured BELOW the global value would still hit the bounce this was originally filed against. Not touched by GL-2/GL-3's melee-approach clamp (CopNpcFactory.meleeFor), which reads tier.cuffRadius() correctly but only affects the standoff distance, not this gate.

title: Cop tier Health was parsed but never applied to the spawned entity
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, commit 93fdacbd): CopNpcFactory.applyHealthBonus(Entity, double), mirroring the civilians helper, sets XAttribute.MAX_HEALTH and current health right after the CopNpc is constructed and before equip()
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-3 fixer round] CopTierConfig.health() was read from cops.yml but nothing ever called an attribute setter, so every cop tier spawned at Bukkit's default 20 HP regardless of its configured Health; retreat-to-cover's Health_Fraction trigger was therefore working off the wrong baseline. Civilians already applied CivilianTypeConfig.health() the same way; cops were the gap.

title: Vanilla CROSSBOW cops fired half as often as before under the Bartizan-matched fire-rate multiplier
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, commit 0a9a62ac): new gangland-api NpcFireRate.scale halves the multiplier for the vanilla bow/crossbow fallback (which Keystone waits 30 x scale server ticks for, against an SPI weapon's serverTicks / scale), so Fire_Rate_Multiplier = 1 / AI_Tick_Rate reproduces 0.11's cadence on both paths; both factories apply tuning after the ranged attack is resolved
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-5 review r1] One per-tier multiplier scaled both weapon paths; the shipped cop multiplier (0.1) reproduced Bartizan's gun cadence exactly but left CROSSBOW cops firing every 300 server ticks instead of 150 (civilians 600 vs 300), halving time-to-kill against owner decision 3.

title: A backup cop sent home could be pulled straight back by the very next radio call
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, commit 2fff005b, owner decision 6): CopManager.responders() now skips the calling cop's own group entirely (`if (group == call.group()) continue;`), so only cops of OTHER groups answer a radio call
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-3 fixer round] The original spec made every RETURNING cop in ANY group eligible, including a surplus backup cop the same group had just sent home; a hunt with frequent contacts could keep it bouncing between leaving and rejoining, bounded only by Contact's cooldown and Responder_Max.

title: A cop killed while walking home (RETURNING) gives no Officer down line and requests no backup
fix: ReturningBehavior.onEnter already calls leaveSquad(), so by the time onCopDeath runs neither cop.getCurrentSquad() nor group.getSquad().members() still contains the cop; a RETURNING-aware fallback (e.g. squad the cop was last in, kept until destroy()) is needed for onCopDeath to still call memberDown
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-3 fixer round; verified still present with T-111's fix in place] T-111 fixed the isValid() lookup gate itself, but a cop that had already transitioned to RETURNING before dying has no squad membership left for either memberDown branch to find, so the death produces no radio line and triggers no backup even though the group is now one cop short.

title: documentation/developer/cops-n-crooks.md still shows non-existent lowercase config keys in several sections
fix: The GL-5 docs pass (commit 804e2b15) rewrote the Cop Behavior/Civilian/civilians.yml example blocks with real Capitalized_Underscore keys in some sections but left others (around the Max_Cops_Per_Player, weapon pool and combat-enabled examples) still showing max_cops_per_player / weapon_name_pool / combat_enabled; sweep the rest of the file the same way
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-5 fixer round 1, still present after that round's own partial fix] The real loaders read Capitalized_Underscore keys under Cops.Behaviour / Types / AI.Combat; these stale lowercase examples predate the loaders and mislead a reader following them literally.

observation: [found 2026-09-27, programme diagnosis] Previously read 'gangland-features/cops-n-crooks' / 'org.luckyraven.gangland.copsncrooks.npc.civilian.*', which only ever existed under stale .claude/worktrees paths, not the active module tree; a developer or agent trusting the header would search the wrong module first.

title: Lieutenant-tier (ranged, Skip_Cuffing: false) cops now sometimes cuff and jail a passive wanted player
fix: Not fixed; flagged for an owner decision. Probably a side effect of move-while-firing bringing ranged shooters inside Cuff_Radius, where they previously froze at the band edge and only shot. It may be desirable (it matches the tier's Skip_Cuffing: false intent) but was not called out in the migration notes as a deliberate behaviour change
tests: Sandbox 2026-09-28: 2 of 6 trials on 0.12 vs 0 of 6 on 0.11
location: gangland-features/cops-n-crooks: npc/police/state/behavior/PursuingBehavior.java (the PURSUING -> CUFFING gate at cuffRadius) together with Keystone 1.13.0's formation/strafe posts
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-5 fixer round 2] SWAT and Military (Skip_Cuffing: true) never cuffed in the same trials, so the change is specific to melee-capable-but-not-forced tiers reaching their now-closer engage posts.

title: Melee cop tiers now kill about 1.6-2.2x faster than 0.11 under the shipped defaults
fix: Owner-deferred balance call, documented in migration §5 and §9; Cops.Behaviour.Attack_Cooldown_Ticks: 50 gets roughly the 0.11 melee pace back (the shipped default, 20, was not changed)
tests: Sandbox time-to-kill: Officer DPS median 0.37 -> 0.82, Sergeant 1.08 -> 1.75, first damage about twice as soon
location: settings.yml Cops.Behaviour.Attack_Cooldown_Ticks, read as NpcMeleeProfile.cooldownTicks (YamlCopConfigProvider.java:388-396), combined with Keystone 1.13.0's real server-tick reaction times
observation: [found 2026-09-28, GL-5 fixer round 2] Fire_Rate_Multiplier only restores gun cadence; melee speed moves independently through the now-correct server-tick cooldown math (CJ-08, KS-NP-22).

title: The first cop group of every boot is re-created ~2 s after spawn and loses tier Health, the POLICE mark, armour and weapon
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, f80dd7c0 + d46cfbcf): the new CitizensNpcs.create turns off SkinTrait fetch-default-skin for PLAYER NPCs (cops, civilians; Banker/Trader set the flag in one line), so Citizens no longer despawns and respawns the NPC when the skin named after the tier arrives. Safety net: CopNpc.refreshLoadout re-applies mark, health, armour and weapon whenever the NPC's entity is a different one, copying the old entity's current health (capped at the new max)
observation: [found 2026-09-29, acceptance squad-tactics] Citizens gives a PLAYER NPC the Mojang skin matching its name; for cops that is the tier name (Officer, SWAT), fetched once per boot, and Skin.applyAndRespawn respawned the NPC as a new entity 1.3-2.3 s later. Health, the POLICE mark (entity data container), armour and the held weapon lived on the discarded entity, so the live cop had 20 HP and no gear, and Bartizan kept shooting from the removed entity (BZ-NU-08). Re-acceptance: 0 entities replaced in 17 runs, SWAT max_health 40 on 80/80 reads. Residuals filed separately: T-139 (other NPC kinds keep no safety net); no police skin is set, so cops show the default skin until the owner picks one

title: Cop deaths never reach the radio: no Man_Down, Leader_Down or Backup (0 of 12)
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, 6dd6f4b8): CopListener.onCopDeath runs at EventPriority.LOWEST, before Citizens' own LOW death handler despawns the NPC, so CopManager.findDyingCop still matches the entity; the down signal carries the real death location; a RETURNING cop in no squad is reported down through its group squad (T-121)
observation: [found 2026-09-29, acceptance squad-tactics] onCopDeath ran at MONITOR; Citizens' EntityDeathEvent handler (LOW) fires NPCDeathEvent then despawn(DEATH), so getEntity() was null and findDyingCop returned null. Re-acceptance: 23 of 23 deaths radioed at +0.5-0.6 s, Backup on the first death of a group. Residual: T-136 (the whole handler, including destroy(), now runs at LOWEST)

title: Stand_Down is radioed twice on every wanted clear

observation: [found 2026-09-29, acceptance squad-tactics] WantedEndEvent and the level-change-to-0 both call CopManager.onWantedEnd, so the line reached every listener twice, 0-1 ms apart. Re-acceptance: exactly 1 per clear per listener. The teardown itself still runs twice and the set is not cleaned on quit: T-137

title: A 'Taking the ladder!' / 'up high' Route line is spoken on flat open ground
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, c9bd3ee4; Keystone 475e31c): SquadRadio maps ROUTE to a neutral Route line or Route_High when the goal is 2+ blocks above the member; the ladder line moved to a Climb key driven by Keystone's CLIMB signal; Keystone no longer plans a route for a melee slot walk that merely lagged the moving target

Existing servers keep the old Route list until the file is regenerated: T-138

title: A re-wanted player far from returning cops gets no fresh cops for up to 300 s
fix: Fixed (0.12.0, branch npc-squad-tactics, 5c4ce008): the spawn task ignores RETURNING cops beyond Pursuit.Max_Distance (or in another world) when counting toward the spawn target (CopManager.isStrandedReturning). 0.21.1 (2f6ebc730, owner ruling R3): out-of-view stranded walkers are now released, so the pinned test flipped 4 -> 2; the 'nearby returners still count' half is unchanged, and a re-wanted player far from his returners still gets fresh cops at once

Re-acceptance: fresh cops at +1.9 s (200 blocks) and +1.9 s / all 5 at +5.9 s (100 blocks); was 0 cops for 150 s. Residual: T-131 (the cap) 0.21.1 update 2026-10-27: the residual (T-131) is fixed in 2f6ebc730.

title: Stranded RETURNING cops stay in the group while fresh cops spawn, so Max_Cops_Per_Player stops being an entity cap
fix: Fixed (0.21.1, branch 0.21.1-spawn, 2f6ebc730 + e3380ee7c, merged 92a59a6b7; owner ruling R3): spawnTick releases out-of-view stranded RETURNING cops, so Max_Per_Player is an entity cap for them again; a walker a real player watches (CopSightlines line of sight within max(24, Visibility_Check_Distance) = 48 b, NPCs skipped) is kept but not counted; reengageReturning skips cops beyond Pursuit.Max_Distance. Verified live on 0.21.1: acc5-acc8 spawn-dup-b R3-count PASS; group peak 7 against cap 8 in acc1.

title: A hurt cop in PURSUING never retreats; band shooters never reach COMBAT unless the player attacks a cop
fix: Evaluate retreat.shouldRetreat plus takeCover in PursuingBehavior too (or at the state-machine level), not only in CombatBehavior
observation: [found 2026-09-29, re-acceptance squad-tactics] Retreat is only checked in CombatBehavior; SWAT enters COMBAT only through Skip_Cuffing within Cuff_Radius 4.5 or findNearestCopAttacker. With the band keeping ranged cops at 8-10 blocks, a cop hurt by a non-player source (gang NPC, fire, fall, generic damage) never retreats: retreat-1 stayed at 10/40 HP for 26 s with cover 12 blocks away and 0 COMBAT transitions. Player-caused hurt does retreat (retreat-p2 runs, 8-9 s behind cover).

title: onCopDeath now destroys the cop, clears drops and exp at LOWEST, before Citizens' own death handler and every later listener
fix: Split the handler: lookup and memberDown/squad report at LOWEST while the entity is attached; move destroy() and the drop/exp/keep-inventory cleanup to MONITOR or HIGHEST via the cached dying cop, or handle Citizens' NPCDeathEvent and match cop.getNpc() == event.getNPC()
tests: CopListenerDeathTest only reads the priority annotation

fix: Give CivilianNpcFactory, BankerNpc and TraderNpc the same loadout-on-entity-change safety net (or move it into a shared helper next to CitizensNpcs); the skin-fetch respawn itself is already gone for all four (T-126)

BankerNpc/TraderNpc have no unit tests because NPC.Metadata cannot load without Adventure on the test classpath.

title: Killed cops vanish mid-death: the body is deleted instead of playing the death animation (regression from 6dd6f4b8)
fix: Fixed (0.13.0, branch npc-roles-medics, c76a618d): CopListener.onCopDeath still runs at LOWEST so the squad hears the death while the entity is attached, but it now calls cop.markForRemoval() instead of cop.destroy(); the body stays for Citizens' own DEATH despawn and the group's next removal pass releases the cop
tests: CopListenerDeathTest (the handler tests verify markForRemoval and never destroy)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, owner report round 2 and H13 diagnosis] REGRESSION of 6dd6f4b8 (H12, T-127, the fix that made the death radio work; T-136 logged the same destroy() at LOWEST as a review-time ordering concern). Moving onCopDeath to EventPriority.LOWEST made it actually reach cop.destroy(); Keystone AbstractNpc.destroy() calls NPC.despawn(), whose default reason is DespawnReason.PLUGIN, so Citizens takes the remove() branch (NMS.removeFromWorld + NMS.remove for a Player body) in the middle of the death event and the corpse is deleted with no animation. In 0.11.0 the MONITOR handler was guarded by isCopNpc, which needs cop.isValid() and is always false for a dying entity, so destroy() never ran in-event and Citizens' own LOW handler (despawn(DEATH), which only drops its reference) kept the body. Keystone is not at fault.

title: Citizens PLAYER-type NPC deaths drop no cash: they take the PlayerDeathEvent path and the debit from a missing User returns 0
fix: Fixed (0.13.0, branch npc-roles-medics, a2f7cb15 + 5b7325b5 + b5f4160f): MoneyDropListener has one MONITOR handler that classifies every death (PlayerDeathEvent included) and debits only when the context is PLAYER; GanglandMoneyDropClassifier asks the module source first, returns PLAYER only for a real player and the new MoneyDropContext.NPC for an unrecognised Citizens NPC (money.yml ships no NPC source, so those drop nothing and nothing is minted); CopManager.findDyingCop also matches a despawned body through the Citizens registry and CopsMoneyDropSource uses it instead of isCopNpc
observation: [found 2026-09-30, owner report round 2 and H13 diagnosis] Not an H12 regression: it dates from f6f73626 (2026-09-07, docket US-06, which debits the dead player's balance for the drop). Every Citizens PLAYER-type NPC death fires PlayerDeathEvent: all cops (CopNpcFactory EntityType.PLAYER), 3 of the 5 civilian types in civilians.yml, traders and bankers. MoneyDropListener returned early from onEntityDeath for any PlayerDeathEvent and onPlayerDeath hardcoded MoneyDropContext.PLAYER, passing the NPC as the player, so dropForContext called depositService.withdraw on a User the NPC does not have (UserManager.getUser is a plain uuid lookup), got 0 and dropped nothing. VILLAGER civilians take the EntityDeathEvent path and were the control case that still dropped. A second gap in the same seam: CopsMoneyDropSource used isCopNpc, which needs cop.isValid() and is false for a dying body, so a cop would have fallen to the MOB tier once the routing was fixed. The vanishing corpse (T-140) made the missing money obvious.

title: Cops that cannot reach the suspect are never recycled or replaced closer, and the spawner choice rejects the other floor on the live layout
fix: Fixed (0.13.0, branch npc-roles-medics, on Keystone 1.14.0 - KS-NP-39 and 9f97fc6 - e1f02433 + b119429f + db487c09 + caca3690 + 2d7c1f1f + b1aaf322): a cop that AbstractNpc.millisUnreachable() reports stranded for Cops.Stuck.Recycle_Seconds and that the suspect cannot see (view cone plus distance, never within melee reach on his own level) is recycled; its replacement spawns away from the recycled cop's spawner for Avoid_Spawner_Seconds (CopSpawnManager.spawnNearPlayer(target, tier, allowed, role) over the filtered findClosestSpawnerLocation) and falls back to a ring search that retries with either roof kind within Spawn.Max_Y_Diff
tests: CopManagerStuckTest, CopSpawnManager fallback tests (spawnNearPlayer hands an avoided spawner to the ring, d65b9b2d), Keystone stagnation-clock tests in NpcFormationTest
observation: [found 2026-09-30, owner report round 2 and H13 diagnosis] Nothing ever replaced a cop that could not reach its target, and a replacement could pick the same bad spawner. (1) PursuingBehavior's only rotation counted a tick when cop.isNavigationStuck() && !squad.hasFreshSighting(), but Keystone's navigation exempts a cop standing where it was sent (the unreachable-wait spot above the suspect) and one cop's sighting resets the whole squad's counter; CombatBehavior had no stall give-up at all. (2) A rotated cop went to RETURNING, which spawnTick still counted toward the target until Pursuit.Max_Distance, so no replacement spawned for up to Return.Max_Ticks (600 AI ticks, about 300 s). (3) EntitySpawner.findClosestSpawnerLocation dropped spawners beyond Spawner_Max_Y_Diff (16) and ranked the rest by XZ distance only, with no way to exclude an origin; the ring fallback only took spots as indoor or outdoor as the suspect within Spawn.Max_Y_Diff (4) and found nothing on the live layout (spawners at Y=115 and Y=80). (4) Keystone had no per-member 'unreachable for N' signal: NO_ROUTE flapped every 5 s and the verdict was squad-wide. On the live-shaped map every route verdict was an iteration-cap verdict and the first H13 clock ignored those (KS-NP-39). Accepted in the sandbox after the clock reversal (lane STUCK, refix rounds 1 and 2, live-mirrored spawners #1 at Y=115 and #2 at Y=80): the stranded group was recycled out of view, its replacements spawned at #2, reached the suspect and cuffed him 22.7-22.8 s after he dropped to the street; 0 recycles in view within 24 blocks over 71 recycled cops; the cap held (max 3 at level 2). Indoors the ring still places nothing (known limit, KS-NP-46). Follow-ups: T-147 (fixed), T-148, T-149, T-150.

title: The POLICE mark is never removed from a killed cop
fix: Not fixed (harmless): clear the mark in onCopDeath/markForRemoval while the entity is still attached, or make AbstractNpc.destroy run its onDespawn callback for a body Citizens already despawned; the death tests should not assert removeMark until then
observation: [found 2026-09-30, H13 diagnosis critique] Neither the old destroy() at LOWEST (which passed no onDespawn callback) nor the new markForRemoval() removes the POLICE mark from a killed cop, and the later group.release -> destroy(removeMark) skips the callback because npc.isSpawned() is already false once Citizens despawned the dead body. NpcMarkManager keeps marks in a WeakHashMap plus a PDC entry on the dead entity, so nothing leaks in practice; the entry dies with the entity.

title: Traders and bankers are killable PLAYER-type Citizens NPCs and, by design now, drop no cash
fix: Behaviour note, no code change: money.yml ships no NPC drop source (MoneyDropContext.NPC), so a killed trader or banker drops nothing and nothing is minted. Owner decision if that should change: add an NPC source to money.yml, or keep them non-lethal through their invulnerable setting
observation: [found 2026-09-30, H13 diagnosis and review] TraderNpc and BankerNpc create EntityType.PLAYER NPCs and are protected only while their invulnerable setting is on (npc.setProtected(trait.invulnerable()) and settings.isInvulnerable()); TraderDamageListener.onTraderDeath (MONITOR) and TraderManager.onTraderKilled exist, so a killed trader is a supported state. Since US-06 (f6f73626) a killed one dropped nothing anyway; after the T-141 fix the classifier returns NPC for it and it still drops nothing. The owner's default for unrecognised NPCs (traders, bankers, other plugins' NPCs) is drop nothing, mint nothing. [acceptance 2026-09-30, lane drops-names] A trader made killable (/npc vulnerable, despawn, spawn) died and dropped nothing (0 item spawns within 3 blocks); a banker kept the vanilla Invulnerable flag after the same sequence and could not be killed, so only the trader was exercised.

title: With cops-n-crooks absent, civilians are unrecognised NPCs and drop no cash
fix: Behaviour note, no code change: civilian recognition lives in CopsMoneyDropSource and gangland-civilians has no Depends on cops-n-crooks. Either move civilian recognition into a seam the civilians module installs itself, or declare the dependency if civilians are never meant to run without it. money.yml's header already says an unrecognised NPC drops no cash (b5f4160f)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, review of 5b7325b5] The civilians module can load without cops-n-crooks. In that setup a VILLAGER civilian used to fall through to MOB and drop MOB cash; the classifier now sees a Citizens NPC nobody recognised and returns NPC, so it drops nothing (PLAYER-type civilians already dropped nothing since US-06). Accepted with the 'unrecognised NPC drops nothing' default.

title: When a Backup runs out, releaseSurplus sends home the replacement Commander instead of the Backup cop
fix: Fixed (0.13.0, branch npc-roles-medics, e3e58603 + 58cac94b + 14e6378d): a Backup running out sends home its own extras, chosen by role (roles beyond the tier's Squad_Composition first, newest first), and never the group's last Commander, so a replacement Commander spawned mid-backup stays and the squad keeps its leader; the first commit's blanket Commander exemption was narrowed by the other two
tests: CopManagerStuckTest / CopManager backup cases (Commander kept, extras sent home by role)
observation: [found 2026-09-30, H13 acceptance lane roles-medic, refix round 1 (F6)] releaseSurplus walks the live cops newest-first and sends home the first PURSUING or IDLE one, whatever its role. After a Commander dies the newest cop is the replacement Commander, still PURSUING a few seconds after it spawns. In all 4 runs with two Commander kills the first kill's 'Requesting backup' line spawned an Assault as Backup next to the replacement Commander; 29-32 s later the Backup ran out, the second kill's replacement Commander had spawned 2-4 s earlier, and it went PURSUING to RETURNING (l3 Kate #8547, l3b Hank #8560, l3cov Sam #8584). The squad kept the Backup Assault and lost its Commander for the rest of the fight: leadership, orders and Stand_Down fell to the Pointman. Sandbox side effect, not part of the bug: on the flat map the released cop could not route to the live-layout spawner and stood 30-45 blocks out. No fix commit on npc-roles-medics. [fixed in the H13 polish, 2026-10-04: the final roles-medic lane (KS ca347e8 / BZ 55598a5 / GL 563ff351) ran 12/12 with two Commander kills and no Commander sent home.] 0.21.1 update 2026-10-27: releaseSurplus now also serves level drops and new lower episodes (T-435, a8eb1a1a7 + 74358bd36); the last-Commander guard is kept there; reengageReturning calls a leaderless group's nearest walking Commander back first (T-439, a0b016f24, a regression from the call-back by distance); the release cap counts one shared allowance of commanders - 1 across Commander roles, so a protected Commander leaves no release owed (T-441, bc1608591 + 3d3134c4d + ab91f4d11). Status unchanged: fixed.

title: Replacements spawned after a recycle hunt the suspect's stale unreachable last-known spot and are recycled before they can find him
fix: Fixed (0.13.0, branch npc-roles-medics, a606774e): CopManager.recycles reported the suspect's current spot to the squad. Superseded under owner ruling R4 (0.21.1, branch 0.21.1-spawn, efe2ed28f, merged 92a59a6b7): a recycle carries no tip at all (never his live spot, and not a re-tip of the last-known spot, which would collapse the search circle to 6 b on every recycle); the circle keeps widening away from a dead centre and, with no tip-off stamp, the evasion clock runs, so a lead that stays dead ends in his escape instead of a recycle loop. Status stays fixed (the recycle loop is gone), by a different mechanism
observation: [found 2026-09-30, H13 acceptance lane STUCK 2b-ii, refix round 1; accepted in round 2] When the suspect leaves an unreachable last-known spot unseen (pillar P, then the street) the squad's goal stays at the dead spot. Each replacement searched toward it under the standing unreachable verdict, armed its stagnation clock within a second of spawning and was recycled 11-13 s later without ever seeing him; spawner #2 replacements walked north toward the house, away from the suspect 29 blocks east. Engagement then waited on a ring spawn happening to have a line to him: 46, 52 and 78 s after the descent, and none in 62 s in one run. Round 2 (a606774e): contact 19-22 s and cuff 28-33 s after the descent in all 4 runs; street-1/2 cuff 22.7 and 22.8 s after the descent (24.8 s before). Keystone is not at fault: the clock arms only on a verdict about the goal pursued now (KS-NP-42), which here is the stale spot. 0.21.1 update 2026-10-27: R4 ruled the live-spot tip out.

The refill searches the squad's widening last-known circle; a lost lead is handed off ahead along the squad-seen heading (T-416, T-440) and units spawn between him and that lead (T-423). title: Update_Checker.Notify_Privileged_Players does nothing: no code reads isNotifyPrivilegedPlayers(), so privileged players are never told about an update on join
fix: FIXED 2026-10-07 in c2053135 on branch 0.15.1: new @ListenerHandler UpdateNotifyListener (gangland-impl listener/player) on PlayerJoinEvent reads Settings.isNotifyPrivilegedPlayers() per join (so /glw reload applies it), skips when Update_Checker.Enable is false (Gangland.getUpdateChecker() null) or the player lacks the notifier check permission, fetches the latest version off the main thread (UpdateNotifier.updateAvailable/getUpdateMessage), then sends GanglandChatUtil.commandMessage(...) to the player if still online. Deliberately left out: caching the last check result (one SpigotMC fetch per privileged join, two when an update exists) - belongs upstream in Keystone UpdateNotifier if it ever matters (ponytail comment in the listener).

observation: [found 2026-10-07 by the settings-ownership workflow (10 section mappers + verifiers); owner confirmed the key is a live feature, not dead] settings.yml documents Notify_Privileged_Players as "Only privileged players will be notified when they join if there is a new update", Settings loads it, but no production code calls isNotifyPrivilegedPlayers(); the only trace was the reflective placeholder/debug dump. title: Spawner and jail rows in a world that is not loaded at startup are skipped, so the next new row reuses their id and overwrites them
fix: Not fixed: `doLoadAll` skips rows whose world is null (`if (world == null) continue`), and the id counter (Keystone `EntitySpawner.loadStoredSpawners` sets `ID` to the max LOADED id; `JailRepository` sets `JailService.ID` inside the loop after the skip) never sees them. The next `/glw ... spawner add` or jail create takes that id and the upsert overwrites the unloaded world's row. Fix: track the max id over every row (or keep unloaded rows as pending) in each repository; same pattern in CivilianSpawnerRepository, JailRepository, JailExitRepository, TurfPowerupNpcRepository (check whether its ids are generated the same way)
observation: [found 2026-10-07 by the 0.16 spawn-dispatch mapper, verified by the orchestrator against the code] Multiworld server where a world loads after Gangland (or was renamed/removed): its cop spawners vanish from memory and the next spawner created anywhere silently replaces the highest-id one in the database.

title: The IDE build (run config 'gangland_warfare build': mvn -T 8 clean package -Dmaven.test.skip=true) fails: gangland-item and gangland-healthbars cannot resolve org.luckyraven:gangland-core:jar:tests:0.21.2 (test), so no jar is built to deploy
